On later blocks, add the month's new committees with their report deadlines. 20m untimed — bidirectional drill: cover the head column and go subject-to-head down all 25, then cover the subject column and go head-to-subject; then a fast pass naming the constituting body for each. 20m timed — 30 historic questions at 12 seconds plus 10 window questions at 15 seconds. 5m error log — write misses as SUBJECT plus HEAD on one line together, never separately; this topic is a pairing problem and half a pair is worth nothing.

ga-circulars.whatItIs: Regulatory changes from RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA, EPFO and NPCI, plus the exact figures attached to government financial schemes. For this exam a 'circular' is never a legal text — it is a rule with a NUMBER attached, and the number is almost always the answer.
ga-circulars.coreMethod:
1. Understand what is actually being tested. Every regulatory item reduces to five fields: Who issued it | What changed | The old figure to the new figure | Effective date | Who it applies to. You are not reading circulars; you are harvesting numbers.
2. Maintain a LIMITS AND NUMBERS sheet that you rewrite from scratch every month — rewriting, not amending, because rewriting forces recall. It contains figures only: repo rate, SDF, MSF, bank rate, CRR, SLR; UPI transaction limits including UPI Lite, UPI 123Pay and the enhanced category limits for tax, IPO, capital markets, insurance and hospital or education payments; ATM free-transaction and interchange limits; NEFT, RTGS and IMPS limits and timings; the DICGC deposit insurance cover; priority sector lending targets, overall and the sub-targets, noting that they differ by bank type; MSME definition thresholds; KYC periodicity; and the minimum capital requirement for each category of bank licence.
3. Maintain SCHEME FACT CARDS. For every government financial scheme record six fields: launch year | nodal ministry | eligibility age range | premium or contribution | benefit amount | tenure. The schemes that recur are PMJDY, PMJJBY, PMSBY, Atal Pension Yojana, PMMY/MUDRA with its three tiers, Stand Up India, PM SVANidhi, PM Vishwakarma, PMEGP, PM-KISAN, PMFBY, Sukanya Samriddhi, Senior Citizen Savings Scheme, NPS, the Gold Monetisation Scheme, Sovereign Gold Bonds, Ayushman Bharat, Kisan Credit Card and PMAY. The exam asks the AGE LIMIT, the PREMIUM and the LAUNCH YEAR — precisely those three fields, over and over.
4. Maintain a REGULATOR MAP, because 'X is regulated by which body' is a guaranteed question: RBI regulates banks, NBFCs, payment and settlement systems, foreign exchange, monetary policy and currency. SEBI regulates securities markets, stock exchanges, mutual funds, alternative investment funds and runs the SCORES grievance portal. IRDAI regulates insurance. PFRDA regulates NPS and Atal Pension Yojana. NABARD handles rural and agricultural refinance and launched the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme. SIDBI handles MSMEs. DICGC provides deposit insurance. NPCI operates UPI, RuPay, IMPS, NACH, AePS, BBPS and FASTag.
5. Scan rbi.org.in Notifications and Press Releases once a week for ten minutes. You are not reading the circulars — you are reading the TITLES, and noting only those that contain a number, a limit or a deadline.
6. Put every scheduled MPC meeting date into your calendar. Rewrite the rate block of the numbers sheet the same evening the policy is announced. A rate learned in August may be wrong in December.
tricks: Rate-relationship shortcuts turn one memorised number into four answers, and they survive any policy change because the corridor structure holds even when the rates move: MSF sits 25 basis points above the repo rate, the Bank Rate moves with the MSF, and the SDF sits 25 basis points below the repo rate. Memorise the repo and derive the rest — but re-confirm the corridor width at the latest MPC, since the corridor itself can be redefined.

Numbers-only revision. On revision day, do not re-read a single explanation — cover the figure column and recall the figures. The explanation is never asked; the figure always is. This alone doubles the speed of your revision passes.

The social security trio must be learned SIDE BY SIDE, never separately, because they are the most-confused item in banking GA: PMJJBY is life cover for ages 18-50 with cover continuing to 55; PMSBY is accident cover for ages 18-70; Atal Pension Yojana is for ages 18-40. The premiums were revised in 2022 — verify the current premium figures from a 2026 source rather than an older PDF.
MUDRA tier names in order with their loan bands — Shishu, Kishore, Tarun — are asked in some form nearly every year. The names are in ascending order of loan size, which is the mnemonic.

'Which of these is NOT regulated by RBI' questions collapse in three seconds with the regulator map: mutual funds and stock exchanges are SEBI, insurance is IRDAI, pensions are PFRDA. Three eliminations, no recall required.

Drill acronym expansions as their own five-second question type, because they frequently ARE the whole question: PMJDY, PMJJBY, PMSBY, APY, PMMY, PMEGP, PMFBY, NACH, AePS, BBPS, NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI, CBDC, DICGC, SARFAESI, IBC, NPA, SMA, PCA, PSL, PSLC, MCLR, EBLR, CASA, CRAR, LCR, AIF, InvIT, REIT.
traps: Quoting a policy rate from a stale source. The MPC meets roughly every two months, and a rate that was right when you learned it can be wrong by exam day. Diary the MPC dates and rewrite the rate block after every single meeting — this is non-negotiable.

Confusing PMJJBY with PMSBY. Different cover type (life versus accident), different age bands, different premiums, different benefit amounts. This pair is the most-confused item in the entire financial awareness block and the paper knows it.
Confusing the fixed-rate reverse repo with the SDF. The SDF replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the floor of the liquidity corridor, and both names may appear as options.
Misreading the deposit insurance cover as per account rather than per depositor per bank. It covers principal plus interest, per depositor, per bank — the phrasing matters.

Assuming priority sector lending targets are uniform. The overall target and the sub-targets differ between commercial banks, regional rural banks, small finance banks and urban cooperative banks. If the stem names the bank type, the number changes.
Treating an RBI draft circular or discussion paper as a final rule. Draft, final and effective-date are three different stages and the paper quotes the final one.

Assuming a limit applies universally. UPI's per-transaction cap differs by use case — tax payments, IPO applications, capital markets, insurance premia and hospital or education payments carry enhanced limits, and the enhanced ones are what get asked.
ga-circulars.timeTarget: 15-20 seconds per question — the slowest questions in GA, because you must retrieve a specific figure rather than a name. If the number has not surfaced in 10 seconds it is not going to, so flag and move.
ga-circulars.masteryCheck: Blank sheet, ten minutes, no lookups: you write the current repo, SDF, MSF, bank rate, CRR and SLR; the DICGC cover; all three MUDRA tiers with their loan bands; the age band and premium for PMJJBY, PMSBY and Atal Pension Yojana; the overall priority sector lending target with three sub-targets; and the current UPI per-transaction limits including two enhanced-category limits. Zero errors, twice, a fortnight apart — so it is retention rather than recency.
questionPatterns: What is the upper age limit for enrolment under PMJJBY?
The EPFO recently enhanced the auto-settlement of advance claims limit to what amount?
Under the Gold Monetisation Scheme, what is the tenure of a short-term deposit?
Payment and settlement systems in India are regulated by which body?
SEBI recently permitted which stock exchange to exit?
The SCORES portal was launched by which organisation?
The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was launched by which institution?
In which year was the National Pension System made available to all citizens on a voluntary basis?
What is the current Cash Reserve Ratio / Statutory Liquidity Ratio?
Which of the following is NOT regulated by the RBI?
ga-circulars.searchQuery: RBI circulars banking current affairs 2026 monthly PDF limits schemes bank exam
ga-circulars.aiPrompt: Do this in two parts and keep them strictly separate. PART ONE, from your own knowledge but flagging staleness: generate 30 five-option MCQs on the STRUCTURAL banking facts that do not change — which body regulates what (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, PFRDA, NABARD, SIDBI, DICGC, NPCI); the three MUDRA tiers and their ordering; the age eligibility bands for PMJJBY, PMSBY and Atal Pension Yojana; the launch year and nodal ministry of 15 major government financial schemes; the relationship between the repo rate, the SDF, the MSF and the Bank Rate; and full-form expansions of 25 banking acronyms. For every question whose answer is a RUPEE FIGURE or a RATE, mark it clearly as VERIFY-BEFORE-TRUSTING, because those change and your training data may be stale. PART TWO: here is my banking and RBI register for the last six months [PASTE YOUR REGISTER HERE] — using ONLY those facts, generate 20 five-option MCQs on rule changes, revised limits, new portals and regulatory decisions. Provide both keys separately. Finally, give me a checklist of every rate, limit and scheme figure I should re-verify from rbi.org.in and pib.gov.in in the week before my exam.
ga-circulars.bookRef: Banking Awareness (Complete Book for IBPS, SBI & RBI Exams) — Arihant Experts. The chapters on 'RBI and its Functions', 'Monetary Policy of RBI', 'Banking Regulation System of India' and 'Financial Institutions in India' cover the structural framework you need. Medium confidence on exact chapter titles as they differ between editions. Critically: use the book ONLY for the framework and never for the numbers — every rate and limit printed in any book is out of date before it reaches you.
ga-circulars.websiteRef: rbi.org.in — the Notifications and Press Releases pages, scanned weekly for titles only; this is free, authoritative and the only source that is never wrong. Then AffairsCloud's monthly 'Banking & Finance' and 'RBI in News' sections; Bankersadda banking awareness quizzes; pib.gov.in for scheme figures and ministry attributions.
ga-circulars.weightageNote: This block together with general banking awareness is 4-6 questions of the 40, and it is the block that separates bank-exam aspirants from general-GK aspirants. It is also the block most self-study candidates neglect because it is dry — which is precisely why it moves you up the merit list in an exam with no interview.
ga-circulars.blockPlan: 15m concept — rewrite the LIMITS AND NUMBERS sheet from scratch from memory, then correct it against your source; the act of rewriting is the study, not the reading. 20m untimed — cover the figure column and recall every number on the sheet, then run the scheme fact cards for the six social-security and credit schemes side by side, then the regulator map. 20m timed — 30 banking awareness questions at 20 seconds each, from a banking-specific quiz rather than a general current-affairs one. 5m error log — every missed figure goes onto a single 'NUMBERS I KEEP MISSING' card; that card is the last thing you read before walking into the exam hall, and it is the highest-value paper you will own.

ga-rbi.whatItIs: The static-plus-current block on the Reserve Bank of India: how it was created, how it is governed, who runs it now, which statute gives it which power, and what it does and does not regulate. Tested only in Mains GA (40 questions, 50 marks, 20 minutes); no RBI questions appear in Prelims. Most of the content never changes, which makes it the most durable investment in the GA syllabus — the only volatile part is the list of people currently in post.
ga-rbi.coreMethod:
1. Split every RBI fact into four buckets and never mix them on one revision sheet:
   (A) ORIGIN — RBI Act 1934; commenced operations 1 April 1935; set up on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, 1926); headquarters at Calcutta at inception, moved permanently to Bombay in 1937; nationalised with effect from 1 January 1949 under the RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.
   (B) PEOPLE — first Governor Sir Osborne Smith; first Indian Governor C.D. Deshmukh (3rd Governor); Manmohan Singh (15th Governor) is the only Governor who later became Prime Minister; current Governor Sanjay Malhotra, the 26th, took charge on 11 December 2024, appointed for a three-year term. Four Deputy Governors as of August 2026: Poonam Gupta (monetary policy), T. Rabi Sankar, Swaminathan Janakiraman and Shirish Chandra Murmu.
   (C) LEGAL POWERS — one statute per function, listed at §5.
   (D) INSTRUMENTS — the policy rates and reserve ratios, which are drilled in the rates topic but blend into RBI stems.
2. Learn every 'term' fact by its QUALIFIER, not by the number. Section 8(4) of the RBI Act, 1934 provides that the Governor and Deputy Governors hold office for such term NOT EXCEEDING FIVE YEARS as the Central Government may fix at the time of appointment, and are eligible for reappointment. So 'five years' is the correct answer to a maximum-term stem, and 'three years' is the correct answer to a stem about the incumbent Governor's appointed term. Both are true; the stem's wording chooses between them.
3. Memorise the Central Board as a sum: Governor 1 + Deputy Governors not more than 4 + directors nominated from the Local Boards 4 + directors nominated by the Central Government 10 + Government officials 2 = 21 maximum. There are four Local Boards, at Mumbai (Western), Kolkata (Eastern), Chennai (Southern) and New Delhi (Northern).
4. Memorise the MPC as a 3+3. Three from the RBI — the Governor as ex-officio chairperson, the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, and one RBI officer nominated by the Central Board. Three external members appointed by the Central Government for four years, not eligible for reappointment. Quorum is four. The Governor has a second, casting vote only in the event of a tie. The MPC must meet at least four times a year; in practice it meets six times, bi-monthly.
5. Attach each function to its statute: currency issue → RBI Act s.22; banker to the Government → RBI Act ss.20-21; regulation and supervision of banks → Banking Regulation Act, 1949; foreign exchange management → FEMA, 1999; regulation of payment and settlement systems → PSS Act, 2007; the inflation target → RBI Act s.45ZA, under which the Central Government notifies a CPI inflation target every five years. The notified target is 4% with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%; it was first set for 2016-2021, retained for 2021-2026 and retained again for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.
6. Keep an explicit NOT-RBI list, because the commonest GA format here is a mismatch item: insurance → IRDAI; securities and commodity derivatives → SEBI; pensions under NPS and APY → PFRDA; chit funds → State Governments. Note the exception that catches people: housing finance companies ARE regulated by the RBI, from 9 August 2019.
7. Learn the currency-issue detail as a pair, not a single fact. The RBI issues currency notes of ₹2 and above under s.22; the ₹1 note and all coins are issued by the Government of India, and the ₹1 note carries the signature of the Finance Secretary rather than the Governor. Note issue runs on the Minimum Reserve System since 1957 — assets of ₹200 crore, of which not less than ₹115 crore in gold. The ₹2000 note was withdrawn from circulation on 19 May 2023 but remains legal tender; it was not demonetised.
8. Know the subsidiaries: DICGC (deposit insurance, ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank), BRBNMPL (note printing), ReBIT and IFTAS. NABARD (2018) and NHB (2019) were transferred out of RBI ownership to the Government of India — a frequently swapped pair.
9. Refresh bucket (B) once a month and leave buckets (A), (C) and (D) alone once learned. People change; statutes and dates do not.
tricks: Read the qualifier before you read the number. 'Maximum', 'not exceeding' or 'up to' points at the statutory ceiling — five years for the Governor and Deputy Governors. 'Was appointed for a term of' points at the appointment order — three years for the current Governor. One word decides between two facts that are both true.

Store the 1934/1935 pair as a formula: the Act is 1934, operations began 1 April 1935. Answer 1934 only when the stem names the Act; answer 1935 when the stem says 'commenced operations', 'was established' or 'came into existence'.

Compress the location chain into one spoken sentence: 'Started 1935 in Calcutta, moved to Bombay 1937, nationalised 1949.' Three dates retrieved in about two seconds as a single string instead of three separate lookups.

On 'which of the following is NOT a function of the RBI' items, run the NOT-RBI list rather than verifying four RBI functions. One check replaces four, and the odd option out is almost always an insurance, securities or pension function.

On match-the-column items with five pairings, confirm the two pairings you are surest of first. A single confirmed-wrong pair eliminates an entire option in about three seconds, which is far faster than validating all five pairs.

Decide first whether a people-question wants an ordinal or a name. Keep the numbered list short and answer from it: 1st Osborne Smith, 3rd C.D. Deshmukh (first Indian), 15th Manmohan Singh, 26th Sanjay Malhotra. Anything else in that list is not worth the storage.
traps: Eliminating 'five years' as the Governor's term. RBI Act s.8(4) says 'not exceeding five years', so five years is the correct key for a maximum-term stem. Reject it only when the stem asks specifically about the term for which the current incumbent was appointed, which was three years.
Answering '1934' to 'when did the RBI commence operations'. 1934 is the year of the Act; operations began on 1 April 1935.
Assuming the RBI headquarters has always been Mumbai. It was at Calcutta at inception and moved permanently to Bombay in 1937.

Swapping the three nationalisation dates inside one option set: the RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949, the State Bank of India came into being on 1 July 1955, and the first round of bank nationalisation (14 banks) was on 19 July 1969.

Assuming the RBI issues all Indian currency. It issues notes of ₹2 and above under s.22; the ₹1 note and every coin are issued by the Government of India, and the ₹1 note bears the Finance Secretary's signature.

Calling the ₹2000 note demonetised. It was withdrawn from circulation on 19 May 2023 and continues to be legal tender — a stem using the word 'demonetised' about the ₹2000 note is testing exactly this distinction.

Getting the MPC composition wrong by counting six external members, or by counting the Governor plus five RBI officials. It is exactly three RBI members and three external members, with the external members serving four-year terms and not eligible for reappointment.
Saying the RBI does not regulate housing finance companies. It has regulated HFCs since 9 August 2019, and this is the exception that a NOT-RBI question is most often built around.
Attributing NABARD or NHB to the RBI's current subsidiary list. The RBI's stake in NABARD was transferred to the Government of India in 2018 and its stake in NHB in 2019.
ga-rbi.timeTarget: Mains GA gives 40 questions in 20 minutes — 30 seconds each. Settle a recalled RBI fact in 20-25 seconds including reading a five-option stem, and close a match-the-column or 'which is NOT' item in 30-35 seconds. Do not chase 10-second answers here. GA is sectionally timed, so seconds you bank cannot be spent in any other section, and rushing only converts a mark into a 0.25 penalty. Spend the surplus re-reading the two or three stems you flagged as uncertain — that is the only place the extra time can pay.
ga-rbi.masteryCheck: On a blank page in 6 minutes, write: (A) five origin facts with exact dates, (B) the current Governor with his ordinal, charge date and appointed term, the four Deputy Governors, and the MPC's 3+3 with the external members' term length, (C) six function-to-statute pairs, and (D) the NOT-RBI list including the housing-finance exception. Then take 25 RBI MCQs in 12 minutes with 0.25 negative marking. Mastery is 22 or better net, with zero errors in bucket (A) or bucket (C). Errors in bucket (B) are expected and are a signal to re-verify monthly rather than to re-learn — that bucket is the only one that changes.
questionPatterns: 'Under Section 8(4) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the Governor of the RBI holds office for a term:' (a) of exactly three years (b) of exactly five years (c) not exceeding five years, as fixed by the Central Government (d) not exceeding six years (e) until attaining the age of 65 years. Answer (c).
'The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised with effect from:' (a) 1 April 1935 (b) 1 January 1949 (c) 1 July 1955 (d) 19 July 1969 (e) 15 April 1980. Answer (b).

'How many members does the Monetary Policy Committee have, and how many of them are external members?' (a) six in total, three external (b) six in total, two external (c) five in total, two external (d) seven in total, three external (e) six in total, four external. Answer (a).

'Which of the following is NOT regulated by the Reserve Bank of India?' (a) Urban co-operative banks (b) Non-banking financial companies (c) Housing finance companies (d) Pension funds under the National Pension System (e) Payment system operators. Answer (d) — those are regulated by PFRDA; HFCs have been under the RBI since 9 August 2019.

'The Reserve Bank of India was set up on the recommendations of:' (a) the Narasimham Committee (b) the Hilton Young Commission (c) the Chakravarty Committee (d) the Tarapore Committee (e) the Nachiket Mor Committee. Answer (b).

'The ₹1 currency note in India carries the signature of:' (a) the RBI Governor (b) an RBI Deputy Governor (c) the Finance Secretary, Government of India (d) the Union Finance Minister (e) the Chief Economic Adviser. Answer (c).

'The CPI inflation target notified under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act for the period 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031 is:' (a) 4% with a band of 2%-6% (b) 4% with a band of 3%-5% (c) 5% with a band of 3%-7% (d) 3% with a band of 1%-5% (e) 6% with no tolerance band. Answer (a).

ga-rbi.aiPrompt: You are setting practice for IBPS Clerk Mains 2026 General Awareness. Generate 25 questions on the Reserve Bank of India — its establishment, governance structure, statutory powers and functions. Every question must have exactly FIVE options labelled (a) to (e). Distribute across: origin and dates including the RBI Act year, commencement date, the commission that recommended it, the headquarters move and nationalisation (6 questions); governance including the Central Board composition, Local Boards and the Governor's and Deputy Governors' terms (5); the Monetary Policy Committee including composition, quorum, casting vote, external members' term and the notified inflation target and its statutory section (5); function-to-statute mapping across the RBI Act, Banking Regulation Act 1949, FEMA 1999 and the PSS Act 2007 (4); currency issue including which denominations the RBI issues, who signs the ₹1 note, the Minimum Reserve System, and the current legal status of the ₹2000 note (3); and two 'which of the following is NOT a function or NOT regulated by the RBI' items where the odd option belongs to SEBI, IRDAI or PFRDA. Include at least one question that distinguishes the STATUTORY MAXIMUM term of the Governor from the term for which the current incumbent was actually appointed, and make both options appear in the same option set. In the answer key, cite the section or Act for every legal fact, and flag every fact that could have changed after your knowledge cut-off so I can verify it independently.
ga-rbi.blockPlan:
Total build: about 6-7 hours across the cycle, then maintenance.

Phase 1, weeks 1-2 — two 40-minute sessions.
Session A: 25 min building buckets (A) origin and (C) statutes onto one A4 sheet in your own hand, one line per fact; 15 min on 15 MCQs, untimed, then correction.
Session B: 25 min building bucket (D) the NOT-RBI list plus the Central Board sum and the MPC 3+3; 15 min on 15 MCQs, untimed, then correction. Every miss goes on a leak sheet.

Phase 2, weeks 3-6 — one 25-minute session per week.
5 min blank-page recall of all four buckets. 12 min on 25 MCQs — that is about 29 seconds each, which is honest Mains pace, not a stunt. 8 min correcting and updating the leak sheet. Do not attempt to do 40 questions on a single micro-topic in one sitting; past about 25 questions you are re-testing the same six facts and learning nothing.

Phase 3, from September 2026 — one 15-minute session per fortnight.
8 min recall of the A4 sheet, 7 min on the leak sheet only. Separately, spend 10 minutes once a month re-verifying bucket (B), the people, against the RBI's own site — that is the only bucket that goes stale.

Final 10 days before Mains: two passes of the A4 sheet at 8 minutes each. Add nothing new.
ga-rbi.weightageNote: RBI structure and functions is a Mains-only topic — no questions in Prelims. Your planner allots roughly 11 of the 40 Mains GA questions to this block, which sits inside the banking-awareness half of the GA section. GA carries 50 marks toward the 200 that decide final merit. The practical case for prioritising it is durability rather than volume: about eighty per cent of the content is statutory and dated, so it is learned once and only refreshed, unlike the current-affairs half which needs daily maintenance until December.
ga-rbi.bookRef: Arihant Experts, 'Banking Awareness — Complete Book for IBPS, SBI & RBI Exams' (latest revised edition). Use the book, not a remembered chapter number — Arihant renumbers chapters between printings.
ga-rbi.websiteRef: rbi.org.in — the 'About Us' and 'Organisation and Functions' pages carry the Central Board composition, the current Governor and Deputy Governors and their portfolios; 'Monetary Policy' carries the MPC membership and the notified inflation target. Cross-check people facts here rather than in a coaching digest.

ga-rates.topicName: Policy rates — repo, reverse repo, CRR, SLR, MSF
ga-rates.whatItIs: The set of numbers and legal levers the RBI uses to control how much money banks can lend and at what price. Five things are examinable: (1) the LAF corridor — SDF at the floor, repo in the middle, MSF at the ceiling; (2) the two reserve ratios, CRR and SLR; (3) which statute each one lives under; (4) who decides them (the Monetary Policy Committee) and how; (5) the flexible inflation-targeting mandate the whole machine serves. For a Clerk Mains GA paper this appears as short direct-recall questions: a rate value, a statutory section, a definition swap, or a two-statement true/false. It is pure recall — there is nothing to derive, so the entire job is storing six numbers and five sections in a form you can retrieve in twenty seconds.
ga-rates.coreMethod:
1. LEARN THE CORRIDOR AS A PICTURE, NOT AS THREE FACTS. Draw a vertical line. Repo sits in the middle. SDF sits 25 bps BELOW it (the floor — the rate banks earn for parking surplus cash with RBI, uncollateralised). MSF sits 25 bps ABOVE it (the ceiling — the rate banks pay to borrow overnight beyond their normal limit). The corridor is symmetric and 50 bps wide. Once you hold the picture, you only memorise ONE number and derive the other two.

2. MEMORISE THE RATE CARD AS A SINGLE SPOKEN LINE. As announced at the MPC meeting of 3–5 June 2026 (61st meeting, rates held, stance neutral): 'Repo five-two-five, SDF five flat, MSF and Bank Rate five-five-oh, CRR three, SLR eighteen.' That is Repo 5.25%, SDF 5.00%, MSF 5.50%, Bank Rate 5.50%, CRR 3.00%, SLR 18.00%. Note MSF and Bank Rate are the SAME number and have been aligned since 2012 — that is one fewer thing to store.

3. RE-VERIFY BEFORE YOU TRUST IT. The MPC met again in the first week of August 2026 and meets roughly bi-monthly after that, so at least two more decisions land before the 27 December Mains. Pull the meeting calendar from rbi.org.in, put the dates in your phone, and on each announcement day spend three minutes overwriting your rate line. Do not carry a stale number into December.

4. FIX THE DIRECTION OF EACH RATE. Repo: RBI lends to banks against government securities. Reverse repo / SDF: banks lend to (park with) RBI. MSF: banks borrow overnight from RBI against securities from their own SLR holdings, and are allowed to dip into the SLR portfolio to do it. Bank Rate: the long-term rate at which RBI lends without a repurchase agreement; today it is also the penal rate charged for CRR/SLR shortfalls. Say the direction out loud every time you say the number.

5. KNOW WHY REVERSE REPO IS A TRAP AND HANDLE IT EXPLICITLY. On 8 April 2022 the RBI made the Standing Deposit Facility the floor of the corridor. The old fixed-rate reverse repo has been dormant in routine operations ever since, though it still appears on RBI's rate table. So a question saying 'the floor of the LAF corridor' means SDF (5.00%); a question naming 'the fixed reverse repo rate' means the dormant figure on the rate table. Check that figure on rbi.org.in yourself and write it next to your rate line — do not assume the two are the same number.

6. SEPARATE CRR FROM SLR ON FOUR AXES. Form: CRR must be held as cash with the RBI; SLR may be held as cash, gold, or unencumbered approved securities with the bank itself. Interest: CRR earns the bank nothing; SLR assets earn whatever the securities yield. Statute: CRR under Section 42(1) of the RBI Act 1934; SLR under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act 1949. Base: BOTH are computed on Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL), not on deposits, not on advances. Write these four rows as a 2-column table — the exam tests exactly these contrasts.

7. STORE THE CEILING/FLOOR LAW CORRECTLY. SLR has a statutory maximum of 40% under the Banking Regulation Act. CRR has NO statutory floor or ceiling any more — the old 3%–15% band was removed by amendment in 2006, so the RBI may set any CRR it chooses. The current 3.00% arrived through four 25-bps tranches announced on 6 June 2025 and effective from the fortnights beginning 6 September, 4 October, 1 November and 29 November 2025.

8. MEMORISE THE MPC IN ONE BLOCK. Six members: three from the RBI (Governor as ex-officio Chairperson, one Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one officer nominated by the Central Board) and three external members appointed by the Central Government. External members serve four years and are NOT eligible for re-appointment. Quorum is four, and at least one of the four must be the Governor or the Deputy Governor. Decisions are by majority; in a tie the Governor has a second, casting vote. Statutory basis: Section 45ZB of the RBI Act. The MPC must meet at least four times a year; in practice it meets six times.

9. ATTACH THE INFLATION MANDATE. Under Section 45ZA the Central Government, in consultation with the RBI, notifies the inflation target every five years. On 25 March 2026 the Government notified 4% CPI inflation with a tolerance band of +/- 2 percentage points (i.e. 2%–6%) for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031 — the second such five-year extension after the 2021–2026 notification. Failure is defined as headline CPI staying outside the 2%–6% band for three consecutive quarters, on which the RBI must report to the Government explaining causes and remedial action.

10. DRILL RETRIEVAL, NOT READING. Every third day, on a blank sheet, write the six-number rate line, the four-row CRR/SLR table, the five statutory sections (RBI Act 8, 42(1), 45ZA, 45ZB; BR Act 24) and the MPC composition. Ninety seconds, no notes. Reading the page again feels productive and is not; writing it blank is what builds the twenty-second retrieval you need in the Mains GA section.
tricks: Derive instead of memorise: store the repo rate only, then SDF = repo − 0.25 and MSF = repo + 0.25. When the MPC changes the repo, all three move together and you rewrite one number instead of three. This turns every future policy update into a ten-second edit.

Collapse MSF and Bank Rate into one entry. They have been kept equal since 2012, so a five-item rate list is really a four-item list. If an option pair shows MSF and Bank Rate as different numbers, you can drop that option without further work.

Bind each statutory section to its keyword so retrieval is one hop, not two: 'forty-two, one — cash' (CRR, RBI Act), 'twenty-four — securities' (SLR, BR Act), 'forty-five-Z-A — target' (inflation target), 'forty-five-Z-B — committee' (MPC), 'eight — Governor' (appointment). Chanting the pair costs six seconds and removes the most common source of a wrong section answer.

Use the base test to kill wrong options fast: both CRR and SLR are on NDTL. Any option that computes either ratio on 'total deposits', 'time deposits only' or 'total advances' is wrong on definition, no arithmetic needed.

Keep a dated rate card — write '5 June 2026 MPC' at the top of your card. When a question in a mock gives a different value, you can tell instantly whether the mock is stale or you are, instead of losing five minutes to doubt.
traps: 'Reverse repo rate' versus 'floor of the LAF corridor'. Since 8 April 2022 the SDF (5.00%) is the operative floor while the fixed-rate reverse repo sits dormant on RBI's rate table at a much lower figure. A stem asking for the corridor floor and a stem asking for the fixed reverse repo rate want different numbers, and both numbers will appear among the five options. Read which words the stem actually uses before you pick.

Interest reversal on CRR and SLR. CRR balances with the RBI earn the bank nothing; SLR is held in the bank's own approved securities and gold, which do earn a return. Option sets routinely offer the statement with the two swapped, and it reads perfectly plausible.

The stale CRR band. Many older study notes still say CRR must lie between 3% and 15%. That statutory band was removed by amendment in 2006 — the RBI can now set any CRR. The 40% figure is the SLR maximum under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, not a CRR figure. An option that puts a statutory ceiling on CRR, or a floor of 25% on SLR, is testing exactly this stale reading.

MSF versus Bank Rate definitions. Both are 5.50%, which makes aspirants assume they are the same instrument. MSF is overnight, collateralised, and lets a bank dip into its own SLR securities to borrow; the Bank Rate is the rate at which RBI lends without a repurchase agreement and is the penal rate applied to CRR and SLR shortfalls. Questions give the right number attached to the wrong definition.

MPC arithmetic. Six members, not seven; three RBI plus three external, not four plus two; quorum four, not three. The Governor's extra vote exists ONLY to break a tie — an option saying the Governor has a veto, or two votes at every meeting, is wrong. External members serve four years with no re-appointment, which is different from the Governor's terms.

NDTL versus 'deposits'. Both ratios are on Net Demand and Time Liabilities. A stem that says 'CRR is x% of a bank's total deposits' has already misstated the base, so any numeric option is unreachable — the answerable version always says NDTL.
ga-rates.timeTarget: 20–30 seconds per question in Mains GA. These are recall questions with no working; if you are still reasoning at 30 seconds you do not have the fact, so mark and move — 40 questions in 20 minutes gives you an average of 30 seconds and GA is where you bank the time the other sections need.
ga-rates.masteryCheck: On a blank sheet, in 90 seconds and with no notes, write: (a) the six-number rate line with the corridor drawn as a vertical picture; (b) the four-row CRR-versus-SLR table (form, interest, statute, base); (c) five statutory sections mapped to their subject; (d) MPC composition, quorum, tie-break rule and external-member term; (e) the current inflation target, band, notification date and five-year window. You own the topic when you produce all five blocks with zero errors on three separate attempts at least three days apart, and when you can restate the rate line correctly within 24 hours of the next MPC announcement.
questionPatterns: Direct value: 'As on the latest RBI monetary policy review, the Standing Deposit Facility rate stands at — (a) 4.75% (b) 5.00% (c) 5.25% (d) 5.50% (e) 5.75%'. Answer (b) 5.00% per the June 2026 review; re-verify after each MPC.

Statute mapping: 'Cash Reserve Ratio is maintained under which provision? (a) Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (b) Section 42(1) of the RBI Act, 1934 (c) Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, 1934 (d) Section 17 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (e) Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949'. Answer (b).

Definition swap: 'Which statement about the Marginal Standing Facility is correct? (a) It is the rate at which banks park surplus funds with the RBI (b) It is the floor of the LAF corridor (c) Banks may borrow overnight under it by dipping into their SLR holdings (d) It is set 25 bps below the repo rate (e) It applies only to cooperative banks'. Answer (c).

Two-statement true/false: 'I. CRR balances earn interest from the RBI. II. Both CRR and SLR are computed on Net Demand and Time Liabilities. (a) Only I (b) Only II (c) Both (d) Neither (e) Cannot be determined'. Answer (b).

Composition recall: 'The Monetary Policy Committee consists of — (a) 4 members, all from the RBI (b) 6 members, 3 from RBI and 3 external (c) 6 members, 4 from RBI and 2 external (d) 7 members chaired by the Finance Minister (e) 5 members appointed by the Central Board'. Answer (b).

Mandate recall: 'The inflation target notified for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031 is — (a) 4% with a band of +/- 1% (b) 4% with a band of +/- 2% (c) 5% with a band of +/- 2% (d) 2% with a band of +/- 2% (e) 6% with no band'. Answer (b).
ga-rates.searchQuery: RBI current policy rates repo SDF MSF CRR SLR site:rbi.org.in monetary policy statement
ga-rates.aiPrompt:
You are setting General Awareness questions for IBPS Clerk Mains 2026 (banking awareness half). Do not ask me for any input before you begin.

STEP 1 — Print a dated rate card first. Table with columns: Rate/Ratio | Current value | Statutory provision | One-line definition | Date of the MPC decision or notification that set it. Cover: Repo, Standing Deposit Facility, Marginal Standing Facility, Bank Rate, fixed reverse repo, CRR, SLR, and the current inflation target with its five-year window. Tag any row you are not fully confident about with [VERIFY] and name the exact page on rbi.org.in I should check.

STEP 2 — Using ONLY the rows you did not tag, write 15 multiple-choice questions. HARD FORMAT RULE: exactly FIVE options labelled (a), (b), (c), (d), (e) on every single question. IBPS Clerk papers have five options — never produce four. Mix the types: 5 direct-value questions, 4 statute-mapping questions, 3 definition-swap questions where one option attaches a correct number to the wrong instrument, 2 two-statement true/false questions, 1 question on MPC composition or the tie-break rule.

STEP 3 — Give an answer key. For each question, one line naming the fact, its statutory provision where applicable, and the date it was decided. For the definition-swap questions, also name which instrument the tempting wrong option actually describes.

STEP 4 — Reprint every [VERIFY] row as a short checklist headed 'Confirm these yourself on rbi.org.in before you rely on them'.

Do not include any guessing advice, elimination-by-frequency advice, or 'the answer is usually' statements. Every question must be answerable from a stated fact.
ga-rates.blockPlan: First pass costs about 75 minutes total, split across two days inside your 45-minute daily GA block. Day 1, 45 min: draw the corridor picture, build the dated rate card, build the four-row CRR/SLR table, and do one blank-sheet write-out. Day 2, 30 min: the five statutory sections, the MPC block, the inflation mandate, then a second blank-sheet write-out and 15 practice questions. After that it becomes maintenance — a 3-minute blank-sheet re-test at the start of your GA block once a week, plus a mandatory same-day 3-minute rewrite on every MPC announcement day between now and 27 December. Pull the remaining 2026 MPC dates from rbi.org.in in week 1 and put them in your phone calendar; do not rely on remembering that a policy happened.
ga-rates.weightageNote: Zero direct value in Prelims — Prelims has no GA section at all, so none of this earns a mark before 10–11 October. In Mains, GA is 40 questions for 50 marks in 20 minutes, and the banking-awareness portion of it typically runs somewhere between a quarter and a third of the section. This study plan budgets roughly 11 Mains questions to the tier-2 banking cluster that policy rates sit inside; rate values, CRR/SLR contrasts and MPC composition together usually account for 1–3 direct questions in a given paper. What makes it worth an early slot is the ratio, not the count: about 75 minutes of first-pass work covers material that never requires derivation and answers in under 30 seconds. Sequence it early in your GA work so the maintenance loop has time to run, but do not displace the current-affairs register, which carries a larger share of the section.
ga-rates.websiteRef: https://www.rbi.org.in — use the 'Monetary Policy' section for the current rate table and the MPC meeting calendar, and the Press Releases section for each bi-monthly resolution.

ga-banktypes.topicName: Types of banks — PSB, private, SFB, payments, RRB
ga-banktypes.whatItIs: The classification block of banking awareness: how India's banking system is divided, how many institutions sit in each category right now, what each category is and is not permitted to do, and which named bank belongs where. Tested only in Mains GA (40 questions, 50 marks, 20 minutes). It is half static structure and half live count — the structure is stable, but the counts and the category membership change every year through mergers, licence cancellations and conversions, which is where most marks are lost.
ga-banktypes.coreMethod:
1. Learn the ladder top-down, because a mismatch question tests the rung, not the bank: Scheduled Commercial Banks split into Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, Foreign Banks, Regional Rural Banks and Small Finance Banks; Payments Banks sit alongside as a separate licensed category; Local Area Banks and Co-operative Banks sit outside the commercial ladder.
2. Public Sector Banks — 12, after the amalgamations effective 1 April 2020. Memorise the list: SBI, Punjab National Bank, Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank, Union Bank of India, Bank of India, Indian Bank, Central Bank of India, Indian Overseas Bank, UCO Bank, Bank of Maharashtra, Punjab & Sind Bank. Learn the mergers as absorptions: PNB absorbed Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India; Canara absorbed Syndicate; Union absorbed Andhra and Corporation; Indian Bank absorbed Allahabad — all effective 1 April 2020. Earlier: Bank of Baroda absorbed Vijaya and Dena on 1 April 2019; SBI absorbed its five associate banks and Bharatiya Mahila Bank on 1 April 2017.
3. Private Sector Banks — learn them by licensing generation rather than by a total count, because the count moves. 1993-94 round: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank (then UTI Bank), IndusInd Bank. 2003-04 round: Kotak Mahindra Bank, Yes Bank. 2014 round: Bandhan Bank and IDFC Bank, both licensed in April 2014, after which the RBI moved to on-tap licensing in 2016. Old private banks are the pre-1993 survivors — Federal, South Indian, Karur Vysya, City Union, Karnataka Bank, Tamilnad Mercantile, Jammu & Kashmir Bank, CSB, Dhanlaxmi.
4. Small Finance Banks — 11 on the RBI's list as of August 2026: AU, Capital, Equitas, ESAF, Suryoday, Ujjivan, Utkarsh, North East, Jana, Shivalik and Unity. Rules: minimum paid-up capital ₹200 crore (₹100 crore for an urban co-operative bank converting); at least 75% of adjusted net bank credit to priority sector lending; at least 50% of the loan portfolio in loans of up to ₹25 lakh; at least 25% of banking outlets in unbanked rural centres. They may accept deposits without limit and may lend.
5. Payments Banks — the RBI gave in-principle approval to 11 applicants in 2015; six commenced operations: Airtel, India Post, Fino, Paytm, Jio and NSDL. The RBI cancelled the licence of Paytm Payments Bank Limited with effect from 24 April 2026, and the Delhi High Court subsequently ordered its winding up with an Official Liquidator appointed. FIVE payments banks are therefore in operation as of August 2026: Airtel, India Post, Fino, Jio and NSDL. Rules: maximum balance ₹2 lakh per individual customer (raised from ₹1 lakh in April 2021); may accept demand deposits and issue debit cards; may NOT lend and may NOT issue credit cards; must hold at least 75% of demand deposit balances in SLR-eligible government securities and treasury bills of up to one year, and not more than 25% with other scheduled commercial banks; minimum paid-up capital ₹100 crore.
6. Regional Rural Banks — set up under the RRB Act, 1976; the first RRB, Prathama Bank, opened on 2 October 1975 at Moradabad, sponsored by Syndicate Bank. Shareholding is fixed at Central Government 50%, sponsor bank 35%, State Government 15%. Under the 'One State, One RRB' policy the fourth phase of amalgamation took effect on 1 May 2025, reducing the number of RRBs from 43 to 28.
7. Track the conversion pipeline as a separate line, because half-completed conversions are the single most-missed cell. AU Small Finance Bank received the RBI's IN-PRINCIPLE approval in August 2025 to transition to a universal bank, valid for 18 months; the RBI relaxed the mandatory holding-company (NOFHC) requirement by revised guidelines dated 6 March 2026, after which AU said it would apply for the final licence. As of August 2026 AU has NOT received the final universal banking licence and remains a Small Finance Bank. Jana and ESAF are also in the conversion queue. An in-principle approval is not a licence; write the two words separately in your notes.
8. Keep the outliers on the sheet, because they show up as the odd option: only two Local Area Banks remain (Coastal Local Area Bank and Krishna Bhima Samruddhi LAB); urban co-operative banks are under the dual control of the RBI and the Registrar of Co-operative Societies, with the RBI's powers strengthened by the Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act, 2020; their umbrella body is NUCFDC.
9. Re-verify counts and category membership monthly. Every number in §2, §4, §5, §6 and §7 has changed within the last two years.
tricks: Answer permission questions from a two-column can/cannot grid rather than from the bank's name. Payments bank: can take deposits up to ₹2 lakh, can issue debit cards, cannot lend, cannot issue credit cards. Small finance bank: can do both. One glance at the grid resolves any 'which of the following can X do' stem in under five seconds.

Learn PSB mergers as absorptions with a single anchor date. Everything with OBC, United Bank, Syndicate, Andhra, Corporation or Allahabad in it collapses to 1 April 2020; Vijaya and Dena collapse to 1 April 2019; the SBI associates collapse to 1 April 2017. Three dates cover every PSB merger question.

Read every conversion stem for the words 'in-principle'. In-principle approval and a final licence are different events with different dates, and a five-option set will often contain both as separate options. AU Small Finance Bank holds in-principle approval only, so it is still a small finance bank.

Anchor each category count to the event that last changed it. Payments banks are five because Paytm's licence was cancelled on 24 April 2026; RRBs are 28 because the fourth amalgamation phase took effect on 1 May 2025; PSBs are 12 because of the 1 April 2020 amalgamations. If you cannot name the event, treat the count as unverified and check it.

Use the ₹2 lakh figure as a one-word identifier. Any stem mentioning a ₹2 lakh per-customer deposit ceiling is about payments banks and nothing else, which lets you skip reading the rest of the stem's qualifiers.

For RRB shareholding, store the ratio not the percentages: 50 : 35 : 15, Centre : sponsor bank : State. It is asked as a three-part option and the ratio form is faster to check than three separate numbers.
traps: Treating AU Small Finance Bank as a universal bank. It has held only an in-principle approval since August 2025 and had not received the final licence as of August 2026; it remains a small finance bank, and an option classifying it as one is correct today.

Counting six operating payments banks. Six commenced operations, but the RBI cancelled Paytm Payments Bank's licence with effect from 24 April 2026 and the Delhi High Court ordered its winding up, leaving five in operation: Airtel, India Post, Fino, Jio and NSDL.

Reading the RBI's own bank-directory page as proof that a licence is live. That directory can lag enforcement action by months and still listed Paytm Payments Bank after the cancellation. Confirm licence status from RBI press releases, not from the directory listing.
Saying a payments bank cannot issue any card. It cannot issue CREDIT cards; it can and does issue debit and ATM cards. The stem's adjective is doing all the work.
Answering '43' for the number of RRBs. That was the figure before the fourth amalgamation phase; from 1 May 2025 the number is 28.
Confusing the first RRB's date with the RRB Act's year. Prathama Bank opened on 2 October 1975; the Regional Rural Banks Act came in 1976. Both appear as options in the same set.
Assuming the RRB shareholding is an equal or a 50:25:25 split. It is fixed at Centre 50%, sponsor bank 35%, State Government 15%.
Counting 27 or 19 public sector banks. It has been 12 since the amalgamations took effect on 1 April 2020; 27 was the pre-consolidation figure from 2017.
ga-banktypes.timeTarget: Mains GA is 40 questions in 20 minutes, so 30 seconds each. A category count or a can/cannot permission item should close in 15-20 seconds off the grid; a 'which bank belongs to which category' or merger-mapping item needs 25-30 seconds because you must check the named bank against your list. Do not compress below 15 seconds. GA is sectionally timed, so any seconds you save are stranded inside GA and cannot help you elsewhere in the paper — the correct use of a surplus is to re-check the counts you were unsure of, since those are precisely the cells that go stale.
ga-banktypes.masteryCheck: In 7 minutes on a blank page: name all 12 public sector banks; name all 11 small finance banks; name the payments banks in operation and state what changed and on what date; state the RRB count with the date and name of the policy that produced it; and write the can/cannot grid for payments banks and small finance banks side by side. Then take 25 MCQs in 12 minutes with 0.25 negative marking; mastery is 22 or better net. Diagnostic: if your errors cluster on counts rather than on rules, your problem is staleness, not understanding — fix it by dating every count in your notes and re-verifying monthly.
questionPatterns: 'How many public sector banks are there in India following the amalgamations that took effect on 1 April 2020?' (a) 10 (b) 12 (c) 18 (d) 21 (e) 27. Answer (b).

'Which of the following is NOT permitted to a payments bank?' (a) Accepting demand deposits up to ₹2 lakh per customer (b) Issuing debit cards (c) Issuing credit cards (d) Distributing mutual fund products (e) Offering internet banking. Answer (c).

'The Reserve Bank of India cancelled the licence of Paytm Payments Bank Limited with effect from which date?' (a) 31 January 2024 (b) 15 March 2024 (c) 24 April 2026 (d) 1 May 2026 (e) 29 July 2026. Answer (c).

'As of 2026, AU Small Finance Bank holds which status with respect to universal banking?' (a) It has received a final universal banking licence (b) It holds in-principle approval from the RBI but not the final licence (c) Its application has been rejected (d) It has not applied (e) It has merged with a universal bank. Answer (b) — in-principle approval was granted in August 2025.
'Under the One State, One RRB policy effective 1 May 2025, the number of Regional Rural Banks in India was reduced to:' (a) 43 (b) 38 (c) 33 (d) 28 (e) 26. Answer (d).

'The shareholding pattern of a Regional Rural Bank between the Central Government, the sponsor bank and the State Government is:' (a) 50:35:15 (b) 50:25:25 (c) 40:40:20 (d) 60:30:10 (e) 35:50:15. Answer (a).

'Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?' (a) Bandhan Bank — Small Finance Bank (b) Fino — Small Finance Bank (c) Ujjivan — Payments Bank (d) Jio — Payments Bank (e) Capital — Payments Bank. Answer (d).

ga-banktypes.aiPrompt: You are setting practice for IBPS Clerk Mains 2026 General Awareness. Generate 25 questions on the classification of banks in India. Every question must have exactly FIVE options labelled (a) to (e). Distribute across: category counts for public sector banks, small finance banks, payments banks in operation, and regional rural banks (5 questions); the can/cannot permissions of payments banks versus small finance banks, including the deposit ceiling, credit cards, debit cards, lending and the investment norms for demand deposit balances (5); PSB amalgamation mapping — which bank absorbed which, with the effective date (4); RRB fundamentals — first RRB with its date and sponsor, the governing Act, the 50:35:15 shareholding, and the One State One RRB consolidation (4); named-bank-to-category matching including at least one item mixing a payments bank with a small finance bank (4); and licensing history for private banks by generation (3). Include at least one question on the current status of AU Small Finance Bank's universal bank transition, with 'in-principle approval only' and 'final licence granted' both present as options. Include at least one question on the licence status of Paytm Payments Bank. In the answer key, state the effective date for every count and every status change, and flag any figure that could have changed after your knowledge cut-off so I can verify it. Do not present an in-principle approval as though it were a granted licence.
ga-banktypes.blockPlan:
Total build: about 5 hours, plus a standing monthly verification.

Phase 1, week 1 — two 40-minute sessions.
Session A: 20 min writing the 12 PSBs, the merger map with its three anchor dates, and the private-bank licensing generations onto one A4 sheet; 12 min on 15 MCQs; 8 min correction.
Session B: 20 min writing the 11 SFBs, the payments banks in operation with the Paytm cancellation date, the RRB block, and the can/cannot grid onto the reverse; 12 min on 15 MCQs; 8 min correction.

Phase 2, weeks 2-5 — one 30-minute session per week.
6 min blank-page recall of both sides. 12 min on 25 MCQs, which is about 29 seconds each and matches Mains pace. 12 min correcting, updating the leak sheet, and re-writing any count you got wrong together with the event and date that produced it. Cap practice at 25 questions per session; beyond that you are re-testing the same twelve facts.

Phase 3, from September 2026 — one 20-minute session per fortnight.
8 min recall, 12 min on the leak sheet plus 12 fresh MCQs.

Standing task, first Sunday of every month, 12 minutes: open the RBI site and re-verify the four volatile counts (PSBs, SFBs, payments banks in operation, RRBs) and the conversion pipeline. Confirm licence status from RBI press releases rather than the bank-directory listing, which lags. Date every correction on the sheet.

Final 10 days before Mains: two 8-minute passes of the A4 sheet, plus one final count check in the third week of December.
ga-banktypes.weightageNote: Bank types is a Mains-only topic — no Prelims questions. Your planner allots roughly 11 of the 40 Mains GA questions to it, inside the banking-awareness half of the section, and GA carries 50 of the 200 marks that decide final merit. Its distinguishing feature is not volume but volatility: the structural rules are stable and cheap to learn, while every category COUNT has moved within the last two years, so the marks are lost on staleness rather than on difficulty. Budget the learning time once and the verification time monthly.
ga-banktypes.bookRef: Arihant Experts, 'Banking Awareness — Complete Book for IBPS, SBI & RBI Exams' (latest revised edition). Treat every printed count in any book as a figure to be re-checked against the RBI, not as a fact.
ga-banktypes.websiteRef: rbi.org.in — the 'Banks in India' directory lists the current small finance banks and payments banks by name, and the Press Releases section carries licence grants, cancellations and in-principle approvals. Use press releases for status changes; the directory listing can lag by months. For RRB consolidation and PSB amalgamation notifications, use financialservices.gov.in and pib.gov.in.

ga-regulators.whatItIs: The block covering India's three non-banking financial regulators: what each was set up under, when it became statutory, where it sits, who heads it, what it regulates, and where appeals from its orders go. Tested only in Mains GA (40 questions, 50 marks, 20 minutes); no Prelims questions. The questions are almost always comparative — a five-option set that swaps one regulator's attribute for another's — so the topic is learned as a matrix, not as three separate profiles.
ga-regulators.coreMethod:
1. Build ONE matrix with three rows and seven columns and revise nothing else. The columns are: set-up date | statutory since | governing Act | HQ | head as of Aug 2026 | grievance portal | appeals go to. Filled in:
   • SEBI — constituted 12 April 1988 as a non-statutory body by a Government resolution | statutory from 30 January 1992 | SEBI Act, 1992 | Mumbai | Tuhin Kanta Pandey, 11th Chairman, took charge 1 March 2025 for a three-year term | SCORES (SCORES 2.0; the old scores.gov.in was closed on 28 March 2024) | Securities Appellate Tribunal.
   • IRDAI — constituted following the IRDA Act, 1999 | became a statutory body in April 2000 | Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 (renamed IRDAI in 2014) | Hyderabad | Ajay Seth, took charge 1 September 2025 for a three-year term, succeeding Debasish Panda | Bima Bharosa (launched 2022, replacing the IGMS of 2010) | Securities Appellate Tribunal.
   • PFRDA — set up by a Government resolution in August 2003 as an interim regulator | statutory from 1 February 2014 | PFRDA Act, 2013 | New Delhi | Sivasubramanian Ramann | grievance redressal under the NPS Central Grievance Management System | Securities Appellate Tribunal.
2. Learn every year WITH its qualifier, because each regulator has two defensible years and the stem's wording is what selects between them. SEBI: 'set up / constituted' → 1988; 'became a statutory body / under the SEBI Act' → 1992. IRDAI: 'the Act' → 1999; 'constituted as a statutory body / became operational' → 2000. PFRDA: 'set up as an interim regulator' → 2003; 'the Act' → 2013; 'became a statutory body' → 1 February 2014. If a stem carries no qualifier at all, treat the item as unresolved and leave it rather than adopting a rule about which year an examiner prefers — nobody can verify such a preference, because IBPS does not release its question papers or answer keys.
3. Learn the composition of each board as a sum, since 'how many members' is a standard stem. SEBI: Chairman + two members from Union ministries + one member from the RBI + five members appointed by the Central Government, of whom at least three are whole-time = nine. IRDAI: Chairperson + not more than five whole-time members + not more than four part-time members = ten maximum. PFRDA: Chairperson + not more than three whole-time members + not more than three part-time members = seven maximum.
4. Learn the jurisdiction boundaries, because 'which body regulates X' is the most common format. SEBI: stock exchanges, listed companies, mutual funds, brokers, merchant bankers, credit rating agencies, REITs and InvITs, and commodity derivatives (transferred to SEBI when the Forward Markets Commission merged into it on 28 September 2015). IRDAI: life and general insurers, reinsurers, insurance brokers and agents, and third-party administrators. PFRDA: the National Pension System, the Atal Pension Yojana, NPS Trust, pension funds and Central Recordkeeping Agencies. None of the three regulates banks, NBFCs or housing finance companies — those are the RBI's.
5. Learn the schemes attached to each, because they generate the current-affairs half of the questions. IRDAI: Bima Sugam, Bima Vistaar and Bima Vahak. PFRDA: NPS, APY (eligibility 18-40 years, guaranteed pension ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 a month from age 60) and NPS Vatsalya for minors. SEBI: SCORES for grievances and the SMART ODR portal for online dispute resolution.
6. Memorise the one fact that unifies the matrix: appeals from orders of SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA all lie to the Securities Appellate Tribunal at Mumbai, and from SAT to the Supreme Court. This single shared cell converts a hard three-way question into a one-word answer.
7. Refresh only the 'head as of' column. It is the sole cell that goes stale; the other six are statutory and permanent.
tricks: Read the stem for its qualifier before you read a single option. 'Set up', 'constituted', 'became statutory', 'under the Act' and 'became operational' each select a different year, and the qualifier is present in nearly every well-formed stem. Locating it takes about three seconds and removes the entire 1988-versus-1992 and 1999-versus-2000 problem.

Answer headquarters questions from the odd one out. SEBI is Mumbai, PFRDA is New Delhi, IRDAI is Hyderabad — and Hyderabad is the only city that belongs to exactly one financial regulator, so spotting Hyderabad in an option set identifies the IRDAI row instantly.

Use the shared appeals cell as a shortcut. Any stem asking where an appeal from SEBI, IRDAI or PFRDA lies has the same answer — the Securities Appellate Tribunal — so you do not need to identify which regulator the stem is about before answering.

On match-the-column items with five pairings, verify the grievance-portal column first. SCORES, Bima Bharosa and the NPS grievance system are three completely distinct names with no overlap, so one confirmed mismatch eliminates a whole option in about three seconds.
Store PFRDA's three dates as a chain rather than as three facts: 'interim 2003, Act 2013, statutory 2014'. Reciting the chain surfaces all three and lets the stem's qualifier pick one.

Decide whether a scheme question is IRDAI's or PFRDA's from the prefix. Anything beginning 'Bima' is IRDAI; anything containing 'NPS', 'Pension' or 'Vatsalya' is PFRDA. The prefix answers the item without recalling the scheme's content.
traps: Adopting a rule about which year IBPS 'prefers' for SEBI. Both 1988 and 1992 are correct facts under different qualifiers, and no claim about examiner preference is verifiable because IBPS does not publish its question papers or answer keys. Read the qualifier; if there genuinely is none, leave the item rather than pay 0.25 on a coin-flip.
Answering 1999 for the year IRDAI was constituted as a statutory body. The Act is 1999; the Authority was constituted as a statutory body in April 2000.

Treating PFRDA's 2003 set-up as the date it became statutory. It was set up by Government resolution in August 2003 as an interim regulator and became a statutory body only on 1 February 2014 under the PFRDA Act, 2013.
Placing IRDAI in Mumbai or New Delhi. IRDAI is headquartered at Hyderabad; SEBI is at Mumbai and PFRDA is at New Delhi, and all three cities appear in the same option set.
Assigning commodity derivatives to a separate regulator. The Forward Markets Commission was merged into SEBI on 28 September 2015, so commodity derivatives are SEBI's.

Assuming appeals from IRDAI or PFRDA go to a body other than SAT. All three regulators' orders are appealable to the Securities Appellate Tribunal, and only from SAT does an appeal go to the Supreme Court.

Attributing a grievance portal to the wrong regulator. SCORES belongs to SEBI, Bima Bharosa to IRDAI. The names are distinct enough that a swap is caught instantly if you have stored the column, and missed entirely if you have not.
ga-regulators.timeTarget: Mains GA gives 30 seconds per question. A single-cell regulator item — headquarters, head, portal, appeal body — should close in 15-20 seconds once the matrix is memorised. A match-the-column or 'which of the following is correctly matched' item needs 25-30 seconds because you must verify two pairings before eliminating. Do not compress below 15 seconds: the year questions turn on one qualifying word in the stem, and skimming past that word is the single commonest way to lose this mark.
ga-regulators.masteryCheck: Reproduce the full three-by-seven matrix on a blank page in 6 minutes with every cell filled and no column omitted. Then answer 20 MCQs in 9 minutes with 0.25 negative marking; mastery is 18 or better net, with zero errors on the appeals column and zero errors on the headquarters column. Separately, take 10 year-questions where the stem's qualifier varies — 'set up' versus 'became statutory' versus 'under the Act' — and score 10 out of 10. If you drop marks there, the problem is that you have memorised years without their qualifiers; rewrite that column as year-plus-qualifier pairs and retest.
questionPatterns: 'The Securities and Exchange Board of India was given statutory status with effect from:' (a) 12 April 1988 (b) 30 January 1992 (c) 4 April 1993 (d) 1 April 1995 (e) 28 September 2015. Answer (b) — SEBI was constituted as a non-statutory body in 1988 and became statutory in 1992.
'The headquarters of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India is located at:' (a) Mumbai (b) New Delhi (c) Hyderabad (d) Chennai (e) Bengaluru. Answer (c).

'The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority became a statutory body with effect from:' (a) August 2003 (b) 19 September 2013 (c) 1 February 2014 (d) 1 April 2014 (e) 1 January 2015. Answer (c) — under the PFRDA Act, 2013.

'An appeal against an order of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India lies to:' (a) the High Court (b) the Securities Appellate Tribunal (c) the National Company Law Tribunal (d) the Insurance Ombudsman (e) the Supreme Court directly. Answer (b).

'Which of the following pairs of regulator and grievance redressal portal is correctly matched?' (a) SEBI — Bima Bharosa (b) IRDAI — SCORES (c) RBI — SCORES (d) IRDAI — Bima Bharosa (e) PFRDA — SCORES. Answer (d).

'Regulation of commodity derivatives markets in India was transferred to SEBI on the merger of which body with SEBI in 2015?' (a) Forward Markets Commission (b) Competition Commission of India (c) Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (d) Financial Stability and Development Council (e) Board for Financial Supervision. Answer (a).
'Under the Atal Pension Yojana regulated by PFRDA, the eligible age for enrolment is:' (a) 18 to 35 years (b) 18 to 40 years (c) 21 to 45 years (d) 25 to 50 years (e) 18 to 60 years. Answer (b).

Every question must have exactly FIVE options labelled (a) to (e). ga-regulators.blockPlan:
Total build: about 4 hours, then maintenance.

Phase 1, one 50-minute session.
25 min: draw the three-by-seven matrix on one A4 sheet and fill every cell by hand, writing each year together with its qualifier in the same box — '1988 (set up)', '1992 (statutory)'. Never write a bare year.
15 min: 20 MCQs across the matrix, untimed.
10 min: correct, and rewrite any cell you missed in a different colour.

Phase 2, one 40-minute session, two days later.
15 min: add the jurisdiction lists and the scheme names to the reverse of the sheet, grouped by regulator.
15 min: 25 MCQs at 28 seconds each, timed, scored with 0.25 negative marking so you practise leaving genuine blanks.
10 min: correction and leak sheet.

Phase 3, weeks 2-6 — one 25-minute session per week.
6 min blank-page reconstruction of the full matrix. 12 min on 25 MCQs at Mains pace. 7 min correcting and re-verifying the 'head as of' column, which is the only cell that goes stale. Cap the session at 25 questions; the fact pool here is under seventy items and a longer sitting only re-asks them.

Phase 4, from September 2026 — one 15-minute session per fortnight: 6 min matrix recall, 9 min on leak-sheet items plus any regulator news from the month. Re-verify the three heads once a month against the regulators' own sites.

Final 10 days before Mains: two 6-minute passes of the matrix. Add nothing new.
ga-regulators.weightageNote: Regulators is a Mains-only topic with no Prelims presence. Your planner allots roughly 11 of the 40 Mains GA questions to this block, which sits in the banking-awareness half of a section worth 50 of the 200 merit-deciding marks. Two honest caveats on how to read that allocation. First, it is a planning estimate from the syllabus weighting, not a count from a released paper — IBPS does not publish question papers or answer keys, so any claim that a specific question appeared in a specific past Clerk Mains is unverifiable and should not be used to justify time allocation. Second, the block's real advantage is structural: six of the seven matrix columns are statutory and never change, so it is learned once in about four hours and thereafter costs fifteen minutes a fortnight.

ga-regulators.websiteRef: sebi.gov.in, irdai.gov.in and pfrda.org.in — each carries its own 'About Us' page with the constitution date, governing Act, board composition and current chairperson.
