ga-devbanks.whatItIs: The four older All India Financial Institutions regulated and supervised by the RBI, each set up by its own Act of Parliament to refinance a sector that ordinary commercial banks under-served: NABARD for agriculture and rural development, SIDBI for micro, small and medium enterprises, EXIM Bank for foreign trade, and NHB for housing finance. A fifth AIFI, NaBFID, joined the category in 2021 for infrastructure. The examinable content is a small, completely static grid: year of the Act, year of establishment, headquarters, ownership, mandate, and the flagship funds or schemes each one actually operates. Nothing here changes, which makes it one of the few GA blocks you can genuinely finish and stop revising — provided you attach each scheme to the right institution, which is where the marks are actually won and lost.
ga-devbanks.coreMethod:
1. BUILD ONE GRID, FIVE COLUMNS, FOUR ROWS. Columns: Act year | Establishment date | Headquarters | Ownership | Core mandate. Do not read about these institutions in prose; prose is what makes the four blur together. Fill the grid once, then drill it by covering columns.

2. LOCK THE DATES WITH THE ONE-YEAR RULE. All four share the same pattern: the Act is one year older than the institution. NABARD Act 1981, established 12 July 1982. EXIM Bank of India Act 1981, established 1 January 1982. NHB Act 1987, established 9 July 1988. SIDBI Act 1989, established 2 April 1990. So you memorise four establishment years — 1982, 1982, 1988, 1990 — and subtract one to recover every Act year. This single rule removes eight facts and replaces them with four plus a rule.

3. LOCK THE HEADQUARTERS BY THE ODD ONE OUT. NABARD Mumbai, EXIM Bank Mumbai, NaBFID Mumbai, SIDBI Lucknow, NHB New Delhi. Two exceptions against a Mumbai default: SIDBI is the Lucknow one, NHB is the Delhi one. Store the two exceptions, default the rest.

4. LOCK OWNERSHIP AS A SINGLE SENTENCE. All four are now wholly owned by the Government of India. The RBI once held stakes in NABARD and NHB and divested both in 2019, transferring them to the Central Government. That divestment year is itself asked, so store 2019 with both names attached.

5. ATTACH THE FUNDS AND SCHEMES TO THE RIGHT INSTITUTION — THIS IS WHERE THE MARKS ARE. NABARD: the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF, created in 1995-96 and funded by the shortfall in scheduled commercial banks' priority sector lending), the Urban Infrastructure Development Fund, the Long Term Irrigation Fund, the Micro Irrigation Fund, the Dairy Processing and Infrastructure Development Fund, the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme (piloted 1992), and the model Kisan Credit Card scheme. NABARD also runs subsidiaries: NABKISAN, NABSAMRUDDHI, NABFINS, NABVENTURES, NABCONS, NABFOUNDATION. SIDBI: the Fund of Funds for Startups (corpus Rs 10,000 crore, announced under the Startup India Action Plan in January 2016) — SIDBI is the operating agency that channels this into SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds, which in turn invest in startups; CGTMSE, the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises, set up in 2000 jointly by SIDBI and the Ministry of MSME; the Udyami Mitra and Standupmitra portals; and, jointly with EXIM Bank, the Ubharte Sitaare programme for export-oriented MSMEs. EXIM BANK: Government of India Lines of Credit extended to partner countries under the Indian Development and Economic Assistance Scheme (IDEAS), and Buyer's Credit under the National Export Insurance Account. NHB: refinance to housing finance companies and housing boards, the Affordable Housing Fund, and NHB RESIDEX, India's first official housing price index, launched in July 2007.

6. LEARN ONE EXPLICIT NON-ATTRIBUTION. The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme is NOT a SIDBI scheme. SISFS is a Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade scheme with an outlay of Rs 945 crore, launched in April 2021, under which DPIIT allocates funds to approved incubators and those incubators disburse seed money to startups; an Experts Advisory Committee oversees incubator selection. SIDBI's startup role is the separate Fund of Funds for Startups. Two different schemes, two different owning bodies, and they are placed together in option sets precisely because they sound alike. Write both lines on the same page so the contrast is stored, not the confusion.

7. FIX THE REGULATE-VERSUS-SUPERVISE DISTINCTION FOR NABARD AND NHB. NABARD supervises Regional Rural Banks and cooperative banks (State Cooperative Banks and District Central Cooperative Banks) by conducting statutory inspections — but the REGULATOR of those banks is the RBI. NHB was once both regulator and refinancer of housing finance companies; regulation of HFCs was transferred to the RBI with effect from 9 August 2019 under the Finance Act, 2019, which amended the NHB Act, 1987, while NHB retained its refinance role and continues to inspect HFCs. In both cases 'who regulates' and 'who supervises or inspects' have different answers.

8. ADD NaBFID AS THE FIFTH AIFI AND STOP THERE. The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development was set up under the NaBFID Act, 2021, headquartered in Mumbai, for long-term infrastructure finance, and the RBI classifies it as an All India Financial Institution alongside the other four. Knowing that the AIFI count is five, and which five, answers a whole question type on its own.

9. DO NOT MEMORISE THE HEADS. Chairmen and Managing Directors of these institutions change and are properly part of the appointments register, not this static grid. If you want them, pull the current names from each institution's own website — nabard.org, sidbi.in, eximbankindia.in, nhb.org.in — and file them in the appointments sheet, where the weekly maintenance loop will keep them fresh. Putting a churning name inside a static grid is how a finished topic silently goes stale.

10. DRILL BY REPRODUCTION. Twice in the first week and then once a fortnight, reproduce the whole grid plus the scheme-attachment list on a blank sheet in under five minutes. Once you clear that twice in a row, this topic goes into the archive and you touch it only in full-length mock review.
tricks: The minus-one date rule: every one of these four institutions was born the year after its Act. Store four establishment years and derive all four Act years. It halves the date load and instantly flags a wrong option that puts an Act and its institution in the same year.
Default the headquarters to Mumbai and store only the two exceptions — SIDBI in Lucknow, NHB in New Delhi. Three of five rows then need no separate storage at all.

Encode each scheme by its owner's initial when you first write it: 'R-I-D-F is NABARD's', 'F-F-S is SIDBI's', 'RESIDEX is NHB's', 'IDEAS is EXIM's'. Scheme-to-institution matching is the dominant question format here, so the owner should be part of how the scheme name is stored, not a second lookup.

Pair every confusable at first encounter rather than learning them apart: RIDF with UIDF (both NABARD, different sectors), Fund of Funds for Startups with Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SIDBI versus DPIIT), CGTMSE with CGFMU (SIDBI-and-MSME-Ministry versus the Mudra-linked fund). A pair learned together costs barely more than one learned alone and defuses the trap in advance.

Answer any 'who regulates' question by first asking yourself 'is the RBI in the options?' — for RRBs, cooperative banks and housing finance companies the regulator is the RBI even though the inspecting body is NABARD or NHB. This is a definitional check, not a frequency guess, and it resolves the commonest wrong pick in the topic.
traps: Attributing the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme to SIDBI. SISFS belongs to DPIIT, with an outlay of Rs 945 crore, and is disbursed through DPIIT-approved incubators. SIDBI's startup vehicle is the separate Fund of Funds for Startups with its Rs 10,000 crore corpus. Both names appear in the same option set and the seed-fund one is the wrong pick for a SIDBI stem.

Act year offered as the establishment year. Because each Act precedes its institution by exactly one year, a question about NABARD will offer both 1981 and 1982, SIDBI will offer 1989 and 1990, NHB 1987 and 1988. Read whether the stem says 'established', 'came into existence', 'set up under the Act of' or 'the Act was passed in'.

Regulate versus supervise, for both NABARD and NHB. NABARD inspects RRBs and cooperative banks but the RBI regulates them. NHB refinances and inspects housing finance companies but the RBI has regulated them since 9 August 2019. An option naming NABARD as the regulator of cooperative banks, or NHB as the regulator of HFCs, is testing exactly this and reads correct to anyone who learnt the pre-2019 position.

RIDF's funding source. The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund is maintained with NABARD and is funded from the shortfall in scheduled commercial banks' priority sector lending targets — not from Budget allocations, not from RBI profits, not from bank deposits. Options offer all four sources.

Headquarters swap between SIDBI and NHB. Lucknow and New Delhi are the two non-Mumbai answers in this set, and options routinely give SIDBI's Lucknow to NHB or vice versa. Storing only 'not Mumbai' is not enough — you need which one is which.

Counting the AIFIs. There are five RBI-regulated All India Financial Institutions: NABARD, SIDBI, EXIM Bank, NHB and NaBFID. An option offering four is the pre-2021 position; an option that includes IDBI Bank is wrong because IDBI was converted into a banking company and is no longer in this category.
ga-devbanks.timeTarget: 15–25 seconds per question. Every question in this topic is a lookup against a grid you either have or do not have; if the grid is built there is no working to do, and if it is not, no amount of exam-hall thinking will recover it.
ga-devbanks.masteryCheck: On a blank sheet in under five minutes, reproduce: the four-row grid (Act year, establishment date, headquarters, ownership, mandate) for NABARD, SIDBI, EXIM and NHB; the fifth AIFI with its Act year and headquarters; at least four schemes or funds correctly attached to each of NABARD and SIDBI and at least two each for EXIM and NHB; the 2019 RBI divestment fact naming both institutions; and two sentences stating who regulates versus who inspects cooperative banks and housing finance companies. Then, separately, write one sentence saying who owns the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme and one saying who operates the Fund of Funds for Startups. You own the topic when you clear all of it twice, at least a week apart, at which point it goes into the archive.
questionPatterns: Establishment: 'The Small Industries Development Bank of India was established in — (a) 1982 (b) 1988 (c) 1989 (d) 1990 (e) 1991'. Answer (d); 1989 is the year of the SIDBI Act and is the planted distractor.

Scheme attribution: 'The Fund of Funds for Startups, with a corpus of Rs 10,000 crore, is operated by — (a) DPIIT (b) SIDBI (c) NABARD (d) NITI Aayog (e) the Ministry of MSME'. Answer (b). The mirror-image question — 'the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme is a scheme of' — has answer DPIIT, not SIDBI.

Headquarters: 'The headquarters of the National Housing Bank is located at — (a) Mumbai (b) Lucknow (c) New Delhi (d) Chennai (e) Hyderabad'. Answer (c). The same set will ask SIDBI, answer (b) Lucknow.

Regulator: 'Since 9 August 2019, housing finance companies in India are regulated by — (a) the National Housing Bank (b) the Reserve Bank of India (c) SEBI (d) the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (e) IRDAI'. Answer (b); NHB retains refinance and inspection functions.

Fund source: 'The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund maintained with NABARD is funded mainly from — (a) annual Budget allocations (b) the shortfall in priority sector lending by scheduled commercial banks (c) the transfer of RBI surplus (d) external multilateral borrowing (e) small savings collections'. Answer (b).
Category count: 'Which of the following is NOT an All India Financial Institution regulated by the RBI? (a) NABARD (b) SIDBI (c) EXIM Bank (d) NaBFID (e) IDBI Bank'. Answer (e).

ga-devbanks.aiPrompt:
You are setting IBPS Clerk Mains 2026 banking-awareness questions on India's development financial institutions. Do not ask me for any input.

STEP 1 — Print a reference grid before the questions. Rows: NABARD, SIDBI, EXIM Bank, NHB, NaBFID. Columns: Act and its year | Date of establishment | Headquarters | Ownership | Core mandate | Three flagship funds, schemes or portals it actually operates. Add a final row of 'commonly misattributed schemes' listing at least four schemes that are frequently but wrongly assigned to one of these five, naming the body that actually owns each — the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme must be one of them, correctly attributed to DPIIT. Do NOT include the names of current chairmen or managing directors anywhere in this grid; those belong in a separate current-affairs register. Tag any cell you are unsure of with [VERIFY] and name the institution's own website page to check.

STEP 2 — Write 15 multiple-choice questions from untagged grid cells only. HARD FORMAT RULE: exactly FIVE options labelled (a) to (e) on every question, without exception. IBPS Clerk uses five options — never produce four. Compose the set as: 3 establishment-year questions where the Act year appears as a distractor, 4 scheme-attribution questions of which at least one uses the Seed Fund versus Fund of Funds contrast, 2 headquarters questions covering SIDBI and NHB, 2 regulator-versus-supervisor questions covering cooperative banks and housing finance companies, 2 questions on funding sources of named funds, and 2 category questions on which institutions are AIFIs.

STEP 3 — Answer key with one line per question naming the fact and, where relevant, what the tempting wrong option actually refers to.

STEP 4 — Reprint any [VERIFY] cells as a checklist.

Do not include guessing heuristics, elimination-by-frequency rules, or any 'the answer is usually' statement.
ga-devbanks.blockPlan: Two sessions and then archive. Session 1 (45-minute GA block): build the five-row grid and lock the dates with the minus-one rule, the headquarters exceptions and the 2019 ownership fact. Finish with one blank-sheet reproduction. Session 2 (45-minute GA block, three or four days later): the scheme-attachment lists for all four, the explicit SISFS-versus-Fund-of-Funds contrast, the regulate-versus-supervise pairs, and NaBFID. Finish with a full blank-sheet reproduction and 15 practice questions. After that, one 5-minute reproduction every fortnight until you clear it twice cleanly, then stop revising it deliberately and let full-length mocks be the only further contact. Total investment is roughly 100 minutes plus about 5 minutes a fortnight — schedule it in the same month as the policy-rates topic, since both are static banking blocks that close permanently and free up your GA block for the current-affairs register.
ga-devbanks.weightageNote: Zero in Prelims, which has no GA section. In Mains, GA carries 40 questions for 50 marks in 20 minutes; this plan budgets roughly 11 Mains questions to the tier-2 banking cluster that development banks sit within, alongside policy rates, bank types and regulators. Direct questions on these four institutions typically run 1–2 per paper. The reason to invest anyway is that the material is completely static and genuinely finishable in about two sessions, so it converts into a permanent holding rather than a maintenance cost — unlike the current-affairs blocks, which never close. Sequence it after policy rates and before the softer scheme-based banking material.

ga-budget.whatItIs: The Union Budget 2026-27 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2026. For IBPS Clerk this is a pure-recall topic: the examiner picks a number, a ministry, a scheme or a tax change from the Budget documents and asks you to identify it among five options. Nothing is derived, nothing is reasoned — you either have the figure encoded or you don't. That makes it one of the most controllable parts of Mains GA, because the syllabus is finite and frozen (the Budget cannot change between now and 27 December 2026), unlike current affairs which keeps growing. There is no GA section in Prelims, so this topic contributes zero to your 10-11 October paper and everything to Mains merit. The verified spine: total expenditure Rs 53,47,315 crore (~Rs 53.5 lakh crore), up 7.7% over RE 2025-26; receipts other than borrowings Rs 36,51,547 crore (+7.2%); borrowings/fiscal deficit Rs 16,95,768 crore; fiscal deficit 4.3% of GDP; revenue deficit 1.5%; primary deficit 0.7%; capital expenditure Rs 12,21,821 crore (+11.5%); nominal GDP growth assumed at 10%; gross tax revenue Rs 44,04,086 crore (+8%); outstanding liabilities 55.6% of GDP with a target of ~50% by March 2031.
ga-budget.coreMethod:
1. BUILD ONE A4 SHEET, NOT NOTES. Everything below goes on a single side of paper in six blocks. You will rewrite this sheet from memory ~30 times before December. Notes you re-read are useless; a sheet you re-write is the whole method.

2. BLOCK 1 — THE SPINE (7 numbers, in lakh crore, learn the two leading digits first, then the exact crore figure for the two starred ones): Total expenditure *Rs 53,47,315 cr (53.5); Receipts excluding borrowings Rs 36,51,547 cr (36.5); Borrowings / fiscal deficit *Rs 16,95,768 cr (17.0); Capital expenditure Rs 12,21,821 cr (12.2); Gross tax revenue Rs 44,04,086 cr (44.0); Total transfer to states Rs 26,20,769 cr (26.2); Tax devolution to states Rs 15,26,255 cr (15.3).

3. BLOCK 2 — THE DEFICIT TRIPLE. For 2026-27 BE: Fiscal 4.3% of GDP, Revenue 1.5%, Primary 0.7%. Comparison row you must also hold: RE 2025-26 fiscal deficit 4.4%, actual 2024-25 fiscal deficit 4.8%. Learn the three 2026-27 ratios as one descending string "4.3 / 1.5 / 0.7" — one object, not three facts.

4. BLOCK 3 — MINISTRY LADDER (2026-27 BE, top four, in order): Defence Rs 7,84,678 cr (15% of total expenditure, the single largest ministry); Road Transport and Highways Rs 3,09,875 cr; Railways Rs 2,81,377 cr; Home Affairs Rs 2,55,234 cr. Fifth is Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Rs 2,39,521 cr. Learn the ORDER first; amounts second.

5. BLOCK 4 — SCHEME LADDER (2026-27 BE, top five, in order): VB-G RAM G Rs 95,692 cr (this replaced MGNREGA under an Act passed in December 2025 and is the highest-allocated scheme); Jal Jeevan Mission Rs 67,670 cr; PM-KISAN Rs 63,500 cr; PMAY-Rural Rs 54,917 cr; Samagra Shiksha Rs 42,100 cr. Also hold: MGNREGS still carries Rs 30,000 cr separately.

6. BLOCK 5 — TAX CHANGES (four items, these are the ones with clean single-number answers): (i) No change in income tax slabs for 2026-27; (ii) Minimum Alternate Tax cut from 15% to 14% and made the final tax; (iii) Securities Transaction Tax raised — options 0.1% to 0.15%, options exercised 0.125% to 0.15%, futures 0.02% to 0.05%; (iv) TCS cut to 2% on overseas tour packages and on education/medical remittances above Rs 10 lakh (from 5%/20%).

7. BLOCK 6 — NEW SCHEMES WITH OUTLAYS (name + rupee figure, both get asked): SME Growth Fund Rs 10,000 cr; Biopharma SHAKTI Rs 10,000 cr over five years; Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme raised Rs 22,919 cr to Rs 40,000 cr; Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme Rs 20,000 cr; Bharatnet Rs 20,000 cr; PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana Rs 20,083 cr; carbon capture, utilisation and storage Rs 20,000 cr over five years; City Economic Regions at Rs 5,000 cr each over five years; disinvestment target Rs 80,000 cr. Named-but-unpriced items to recognise: Semiconductor Mission 2.0, High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat, Infrastructure Risk Guarantee Fund, Rare Earth Corridors in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, seven high-speed rail corridors, 20 new national waterways over five years.

8. DRILL PROTOCOL. Daily, 8 minutes: blank paper, reproduce the six blocks, then check against the sheet and circle only the misses. Weekly, 15 minutes: full rewrite including exact crore figures. The circled misses from the week become the next week's first three minutes. Do not re-read — reproduce.

9. EXAM PROTOCOL. Read the stem, decide within 10 seconds whether the figure is in your sheet. If yes, mark and move. If it has not surfaced by 20 seconds, leave it blank — 0.25 negative marking makes a coin-flip across five options negative in expectation.
tricks: PRIMARY DEFICIT BY SUBTRACTION, NOT BY MEMORY. Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit minus Interest payments. 16,95,768 minus 14,03,972 = 2,91,796 crore, exactly the published figure. So memorise fiscal deficit and interest payments, and derive the third in about 8 seconds instead of carrying a third number for eight months. The same subtraction confirms your memory of interest payments if a question gives you the primary deficit.

RECOVER IMPLIED NOMINAL GDP IN ONE DIVISION. Fiscal deficit Rs 16,95,768 crore is 4.3% of GDP, so GDP = 16,95,768 / 0.043 = approximately Rs 3.94 crore crore, i.e. about Rs 394 lakh crore. Check any 'as a percentage of GDP' option against this: revenue deficit 5,92,344 / 394 lakh crore = 1.50 percent, which matches the published 1.5%. Capital expenditure 12,21,821 / 394 lakh crore = 3.1 percent. This turns a recall question into an arithmetic one when your memory is shaky.

INTEREST PAYMENTS HAVE TWO DENOMINATORS AND BOTH ARE ASKED. Rs 14,03,972 crore is 26% of TOTAL EXPENDITURE and 40% of REVENUE RECEIPTS. Store the pair '26 and 40' together; a stem that says 'of revenue receipts' and an answer key of 26 are the classic mismatch. Reading which denominator the stem names costs 3 seconds and saves the mark.

MINISTRY-OR-SCHEME FILTER BEFORE YOU LOOK AT AMOUNTS. If the stem says 'highest allocation among ministries', any option that is a scheme name (VB-G RAM G, Jal Jeevan Mission, PM-KISAN) is eliminated without checking a single rupee figure, and vice versa. On a five-option Mains question this routinely removes two or three options in under 5 seconds, leaving a two-way call you can settle from the ladder you memorised.

ONE GROWTH-RATE CHAIN ANSWERS ALL 'WHICH GREW FASTEST' QUESTIONS. For 2026-27 BE over RE 2025-26: capital expenditure +11.5% > total expenditure +7.7% > receipts excluding borrowings +7.2% > revenue expenditure +6.6%. Learn the single ordered chain rather than four loose percentages; the ordering itself is what the question tests.

TWO-DIGIT COMPRESSION WITH A NAMED EXCEPTION. Carry 53 / 36 / 17 / 12 / 44 / 26 as the lakh-crore digits for the spine. Because options can be printed as exact crore figures, keep the full precision for exactly two items — total expenditure Rs 53,47,315 crore and fiscal deficit Rs 16,95,768 crore — since those two are the ones printed exactly most often. If two options share the same lakh-crore digits, you must have the exact figure; do not guess between them.
traps: BUDGET ESTIMATE vs REVISED ESTIMATE. 4.3% of GDP is the fiscal deficit TARGET for 2026-27 (BE). 4.4% is the REVISED estimate for 2025-26. 4.8% is the ACTUAL for 2024-25. All three appear as options together. A stem reading 'the revised estimate of fiscal deficit' has answer 4.4%, not 4.3% — candidates who learned only '4.3' mark it and lose 1.25 marks net.

CAPITAL EXPENDITURE vs EFFECTIVE CAPITAL EXPENDITURE. Budgeted capex is Rs 12,21,821 crore (about Rs 12.2 lakh crore). 'Effective capex', which adds grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets and capex loans to states, is about Rs 17.15 lakh crore. Both are printed as options. Read whether the stem says 'capital expenditure' or 'effective capital expenditure'.

THE GST LINE FALLS 2.6% AND THAT IS NOT A COLLAPSE IN GST. Total GST shows minus 2.6% only because GST Compensation Cess drops to zero in 2026-27 (it was Rs 88,000 crore in RE 2025-26). CGST alone rises 6.3% to Rs 10,19,020 crore. A question phrased as 'which tax head shows a decline' is answerable, but an inference option saying 'GST collections are budgeted to fall' is wrong reasoning built on a right number.

MGNREGS IS NO LONGER THE TOP SCHEME. MGNREGA was replaced by the VB-G RAM G Act in December 2025. VB-G RAM G gets Rs 95,692 crore in 2026-27 and is the highest-allocated scheme; MGNREGS separately retains Rs 30,000 crore, a 66% fall. Candidates revising from 2024 material will mark MGNREGS or PM-KISAN for 'highest allocated scheme' and be wrong.

THE Rs 12 LAKH REBATE BELONGS TO BUDGET 2025-26, NOT 2026-27. Budget 2026-27 made NO CHANGE to income tax slabs. The full rebate up to Rs 12 lakh (Rs 12.75 lakh for salaried, including standard deduction) was announced in the previous Budget and merely continues. A stem asking 'which of the following was announced in Union Budget 2026-27' with the rebate as an option is testing exactly this confusion.

THREE DIFFERENT 'TRANSFER' NUMBERS. Total expenditure Rs 53,47,315 crore; total transfer to states Rs 26,20,769 crore; tax devolution to states Rs 15,26,255 crore; interest-free capex loans to states Rs 1,85,000 crore. These are four distinct figures and options mix them. 'Tax devolution' means only the states' share of central taxes, not grants and loans.

FISCAL DEFICIT IS NOT GROSS MARKET BORROWING. The Rs 16,95,768 crore figure is the fiscal deficit, financed by borrowings and other liabilities. Gross market borrowing is a separate, different number published in the Budget documents. If a stem asks for gross market borrowing, do not substitute the fiscal deficit — look the actual figure up on indiabudget.gov.in and add it to your sheet rather than assuming they are equal.

MAT IS 14%, AND IT IS NOT THE CORPORATE TAX RATE. Minimum Alternate Tax was cut from 15% to 14% and made the final tax with MAT credit accumulation stopping from 1 April 2026. Options frequently include 18.5% (a long-dead older MAT rate) and 22% (the buyback effective rate for corporate promoters). Read the tax name, not the shape of the number.
ga-budget.timeTarget: IN THE EXAM: Mains GA is 40 questions in 20 minutes, i.e. 30 seconds average, and GA is the one section where a prepared candidate banks time for the other three. Target 10-12 seconds per Budget question — read stem, recall from the sheet, mark, move. Hard cap 20 seconds; if the figure has not surfaced by then, leave it blank. A five-option guess at 0.25 negative marking is negative in expectation. IN PREPARATION: about 6 focused hours to build and first-memorise the six-block sheet (spread over 3 sessions), then 8 minutes of blank-paper cold recall daily and one 15-minute full rewrite weekly from now until the Mains on 27 December 2026. Total ongoing cost: under 70 minutes a week.
ga-budget.masteryCheck: Sit with blank paper and a 5-minute timer, no prompts. Write: (1) all seven spine numbers to the nearest thousand crore; (2) the deficit triple 4.3 / 1.5 / 0.7 plus the RE 2025-26 fiscal deficit; (3) the top four ministries in descending order with amounts; (4) the top five schemes in descending order with amounts; (5) the four tax changes; (6) six new schemes with their outlays. Then, without looking, derive the primary deficit from fiscal deficit minus interest payments and check it equals Rs 2,91,796 crore, and derive implied nominal GDP from the fiscal deficit and its ratio and check it lands near Rs 394 lakh crore. You have mastered the topic when you complete all eight items inside 5 minutes with at most two misses, on three separate days in the same week. Until then the topic is not learned, only read.
questionPatterns: Direct ratio recall: 'As per Union Budget 2026-27, the fiscal deficit is targeted at what percentage of GDP? (a) 4.9% (b) 4.8% (c) 4.4% (d) 4.3% (e) 4.1%' — answer (d) 4.3%. Note that (b) is the 2024-25 actual and (c) is the RE 2025-26 figure, both planted as near-misses.

Highest-allocation identification: 'Which ministry has been given the highest allocation in Union Budget 2026-27? (a) Railways (b) Road Transport and Highways (c) Defence (d) Home Affairs (e) Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution' — answer (c) Defence, at Rs 7,84,678 crore, about 15% of total expenditure.

Approximate aggregate: 'The total expenditure budgeted by the central government for 2026-27 is approximately (a) Rs 48.2 lakh crore (b) Rs 50.7 lakh crore (c) Rs 53.5 lakh crore (d) Rs 56.1 lakh crore (e) Rs 58.4 lakh crore' — answer (c). Option (b) is the BE for 2025-26, the standard trap.
Single tax-rate change: 'In Union Budget 2026-27, the Minimum Alternate Tax rate was reduced from 15% to (a) 10% (b) 12% (c) 12.5% (d) 14% (e) 15.5%' — answer (d) 14%.

Scheme outlay: 'What is the outlay announced for the SME Growth Fund in Union Budget 2026-27? (a) Rs 5,000 crore (b) Rs 10,000 crore (c) Rs 15,000 crore (d) Rs 20,000 crore (e) Rs 25,000 crore' — answer (b) Rs 10,000 crore. The Rs 20,000 crore option is planted because RDI Scheme, Bharatnet and CCUS each carry that figure.

Scheme-name substitution: 'Which scheme has the highest allocation in Union Budget 2026-27? (a) PM-KISAN (b) MGNREGS (c) Jal Jeevan Mission (d) VB-G RAM G (e) PMAY-Rural' — answer (d) VB-G RAM G at Rs 95,692 crore.

ga-budget.aiPrompt: Act as an IBPS Clerk Mains General Awareness question setter. Using ONLY the Union Budget 2026-27 (presented 1 February 2026), generate 15 multiple-choice questions. STRICT FORMAT RULES: every question must have EXACTLY FIVE options labelled (a), (b), (c), (d), (e) — IBPS papers always use five options, never four. Distribute the 15 questions as: 4 on headline aggregates (total expenditure, receipts excluding borrowings, capital expenditure, gross tax revenue), 3 on deficit ratios as a percentage of GDP, 3 on ministry-wise allocations, 3 on scheme-wise allocations, 2 on tax proposals. SETUP PHASE (one week, do it now, well before Mains): three 2-hour sessions in your GA slot to build the six-block A4 sheet from indiabudget.gov.in and the PRS Union Budget 2026-27 Analysis, and to memorise blocks 1-3. MAINTENANCE PHASE (February to September): 8 minutes at the very end of your daily 4 hours, blank-paper reproduction of two rotating blocks, plus one 15-minute full rewrite on your weekly review day. This sits alongside, not instead of, your daily current-affairs reading. ga-budget.websiteRef: indiabudget.gov.in (official Budget at a Glance, Receipts Budget, Expenditure Profile and Expenditure Budget documents — the primary source, and free); prsindia.org (Union Budget 2026-27 Analysis, a clean tabulated summary of the same figures); pib.gov.in (official Budget highlights press releases).

ga-survey.whatItIs: Two things bundled into one topic because IBPS asks them together. First, the Economic Survey 2025-26 — the Finance Ministry's annual review of the economy, prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs under Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran and tabled in Parliament on 29 January 2026, three days before the Budget. Its stated theme is 'Strategic Indispensability'. Second, the GDP and inflation vocabulary that questions about the Survey and about RBI policy sit on top of: real versus nominal GDP, GVA versus GDP, the GDP deflator, CPI versus WPI, headline versus core inflation, base years, and which ministry publishes what. The Survey's verified headline numbers: real GDP growth estimated at 7.4% for 2025-26 (against 6.5% in 2024-25), projected at 6.8% to 7.2% for 2026-27, with medium-term potential put at around 7%; retail inflation averaging 1.7% over April-December 2025-26 against 4.6% the previous year; current account deficit 0.8% of GDP in H1 2025-26 against 1.3% a year earlier; FDI inflows of USD 81 billion in 2025, up 13%; forex reserves covering about 11 months of imports and 94% of external outstanding debt; private final consumption expenditure at 61.5% of GDP, the highest since 2011-12. Separately and importantly for 2026, MoSPI replaced the base years of all three headline statistics this year.
ga-survey.coreMethod:
1. ONE A4 SHEET, FOUR BLOCKS, REWRITTEN NOT RE-READ — same protocol as the Budget topic, and keep both sheets in the same folder because Mains mixes questions from the two documents freely.

2. BLOCK 1 — IDENTITY FACTS (the cheapest marks): Economic Survey 2025-26 tabled 29 January 2026; prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance; author-in-chief is the Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran (his term has been extended to March 2027); theme 'Strategic Indispensability'; it is tabled BEFORE the Budget and is advisory, not binding.

3. BLOCK 2 — THE GROWTH CHAIN, LEARNED AS ONE STRING: 6.5% (2024-25 actual) then 7.4% (2025-26 estimate) then 6.8-7.2% (2026-27 projection, a RANGE not a point), with medium-term potential around 7%. Attach the Survey's claim that India remains the fastest-growing major economy for a fourth consecutive year. Attach separately the Budget's assumption of 10% NOMINAL GDP growth for 2026-27 — different document, different concept.

4. BLOCK 3 — SUPPORTING NUMBERS (six items): retail inflation 1.7% for April-December 2025-26 versus 4.6% a year earlier, and projected to rise gradually within the 4% plus-or-minus 2% band; CAD 0.8% of GDP in H1 2025-26; FDI USD 81 billion in 2025, up 13%; forex reserves covering ~11 months of imports and 94% of external debt; PFCE 61.5% of GDP; unemployment 3.2% and female labour force participation 42% (both PLFS 2023-24). Sectoral: industry ~7% and services ~9% in H1 2025-26, manufacturing 9% in Q2, agriculture 4.6% in 2024-25. Aggregate state fiscal deficit 3.2% of GDP in 2024-25. Gig workers 2% of the workforce now, projected 6.7% by 2029-30.

5. BLOCK 4a — GDP CONCEPTS. Nominal GDP is at current prices and includes inflation; real GDP is at constant prices. GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) x 100, and it covers the entire economy, unlike CPI which covers a consumption basket. The bridge formula, which is directly plugged into numeric questions: GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + product taxes − product subsidies. Worked example: if GVA at basic prices is Rs 100 lakh crore, product taxes Rs 15 lakh crore and product subsidies Rs 5 lakh crore, then GDP = 100 + 15 − 5 = Rs 110 lakh crore. Second worked example on the deflator: if nominal GDP grows 10% and real GDP grows 7%, the implied deflator-based inflation is approximately 10 − 7 = 3%.

6. BLOCK 4b — BASE YEARS, THE BIG 2026 UPDATE. MoSPI released the new GDP series with base year 2022-23 on 27 February 2026, replacing 2011-12; the new CPI series with base year 2024 on 12 February 2026, replacing 2012; and the new IIP series with base year 2022-23 on 28 May 2026, replacing 2011-12. Methodological changes flagged: use of GST and e-Vahan administrative data, and a shift to double deflation. WPI continues on base year 2011-12.

7. BLOCK 4c — INFLATION CONCEPTS AND OWNERSHIP. CPI (Combined) is compiled by the National Statistical Office under MoSPI and is the measure the RBI targets. WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, and contains no services. Headline inflation is the all-items index; core inflation excludes food and fuel. Demand-pull inflation comes from excess demand; cost-push from input costs. The flexible inflation targeting framework, in force since 2016, sets 4% CPI with a 2%-6% tolerance band, fixed by the Centre in consultation with the RBI for five-year periods; the previous period ran 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026, so CHECK the notified target for 1 April 2026 onward on rbi.org.in before the exam rather than assuming it is unchanged. The MPC has six members, three from the RBI and three external, and the RBI Governor chairs it and holds a casting vote.

8. BLOCK 4d — CURRENT POLICY NUMBERS (volatile, re-verify monthly): repo rate held at 5.25% through the February, April and June 2026 reviews with a neutral stance; RBI raised its FY27 CPI forecast to 5.1% in June 2026; CPI print for June 2026 was 4.38%, an 18-month high. The next MPC met 5-7 August 2026 — look up that resolution and update this line.

9. DRILL PROTOCOL. Daily 8 minutes: blank-paper reproduction of one rotating block. Weekly 15 minutes: full sheet plus both worked formulas computed from scratch. Monthly 5 minutes: re-verify the volatile lines in Block 4d against rbi.org.in.

10. EXAM PROTOCOL. Concept questions (deflator, GVA-to-GDP, who publishes WPI) are solvable and worth 20 seconds. Pure Survey-number questions are recall — 12 seconds, then blank.
tricks: RANGE VERSUS POINT TELLS YOU WHICH NUMBER THE STEM WANTS. The Survey gives a POINT estimate for the current year (7.4% for 2025-26) and a RANGE for the coming year (6.8-7.2% for 2026-27). So if the options for a 2026-27 question are all single numbers, the stem is probably asking for the Budget's 10% NOMINAL assumption or an outside agency's forecast, not the Survey's projection. Reading the year and the word 'range' costs 3 seconds and stops the commonest cross-document error.

THE DEFLATOR SUBTRACTION LINKS THE TWO DOCUMENTS AND SELF-CHECKS BOTH. Nominal growth minus real growth gives approximate deflator inflation. The Budget assumes 10% nominal for 2026-27; the Survey projects 6.8-7.2% real; so the implied economy-wide price rise is roughly 2.8 to 3.2%. If you can only remember two of those three quantities in the hall, one subtraction recovers the third.

BASE-YEAR PAIRING HALVES THE MEMORY LOAD. GDP and IIP SHARE the new base year 2022-23; CPI alone sits at 2024; WPI alone is still 2011-12. Encode it as 'two share 22-23, CPI is 2024, WPI is the old one' — three chunks instead of four dates. If you also want the release dates: CPI 12 February, GDP 27 February, IIP 28 May, all 2026, in calendar order.

ONE LINE OWNS AN ENTIRE QUESTION FAMILY: GDP, CPI and IIP are all MoSPI/NSO; WPI alone is the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry. 'Which of the following is NOT published by MoSPI' and 'which ministry releases WPI' are both answered by this single sentence in under 5 seconds.

THE GVA BRIDGE IS PLUG-AND-PLAY. GDP = GVA + product taxes − product subsidies. Any numeric question of this shape resolves in one addition and one subtraction. Rehearse it in the direction the exam uses more often, GVA to GDP, and remember the sign: taxes ADD, subsidies SUBTRACT, because subsidies are already sitting inside the basic price.

SEPARATE THE THREE 'GROWTH' NUMBERS BY THEIR OWNER BEFORE YOU RECALL. 7.4% belongs to the Economic Survey and is REAL, for 2025-26. 10% belongs to the Union Budget and is NOMINAL, for 2026-27. 6.8-7.2% belongs to the Survey and is REAL, for 2026-27. Filing them under document-plus-concept rather than as three loose percentages is what makes them retrievable eleven months later.
traps: 'FASTEST-GROWING MAJOR ECONOMY' IS NOT 'LARGEST ECONOMY', AND THE SIZE RANKING HAS MOVED. As per the IMF's April 2026 World Economic Outlook database, India's nominal GDP is about USD 4.15 trillion and it ranks SIXTH, behind Japan (about USD 4.38 trillion, fourth) and the United Kingdom (about USD 4.26 trillion, fifth). The slip from fourth reflects roughly 11% rupee depreciation in FY26 and the GDP base-year revision. The widely-repeated 'India is the fourth largest economy' line is now stale — verify the ranking on imf.org before the exam instead of reciting last year's coaching material.

REAL VERSUS NOMINAL ACROSS DOCUMENTS. The Survey's 7.4% is REAL growth; the Budget's 10% is NOMINAL growth. Marking 10% for 'the Economic Survey's estimate of GDP growth' or 7.4% for 'the nominal GDP growth assumed in the Budget' are the two mirror-image errors, and options are set so both are available.

THE 1.7% INFLATION FIGURE HAS A TIME WINDOW ATTACHED. That is the AVERAGE retail inflation for APRIL-DECEMBER 2025-26 as reported in the Survey. It is not the full-year figure and it is emphatically not the current print — CPI stood at 4.38% in June 2026, an 18-month high, and the RBI raised its FY27 forecast to 5.1%. A stem saying 'current retail inflation' and a stem saying 'as per the Economic Survey 2025-26' have different answers.

THE UNEMPLOYMENT AND FLFP NUMBERS ARE 2023-24 PLFS DATA, NOT 2026 DATA. Unemployment 3.2% and female labour force participation 42% are quoted in the Survey but refer to the Periodic Labour Force Survey for 2023-24. Do not present them as the position in 2026, and expect stems that name the reference year explicitly.

WPI IS NOT THE RBI'S TARGET AND CONTAINS NO SERVICES. The RBI's flexible inflation targeting framework is defined on CPI (Combined). WPI covers wholesale goods transactions only — no services, no retail margin — which is why WPI and CPI can move in opposite directions. Options offering 'WPI' for 'which index does the RBI target' are the standard bait.

THE SURVEY COMES BEFORE THE BUDGET AND DOES NOT BIND IT. Economic Survey 2025-26 was tabled on 29 January 2026; the Budget was presented on 1 February 2026. It is an assessment authored under the CEA, not a policy commitment by the government, and its projections routinely differ from the Budget's assumptions. Questions asking 'which was tabled first' or 'who prepares the Economic Survey' turn on exactly this.

THE INFLATION-TARGET PERIOD EXPIRED ON 31 MARCH 2026. The 4% target with a 2%-6% band was notified for 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026 and is reset every five years by the Centre in consultation with the RBI. The framework structure has been consistent since 2016, but the notification covering April 2026 onward must be checked on rbi.org.in — do not state a target period from memory in an exam year when the period rolled over.

BASE-YEAR REVISION CHANGES LEVELS, NOT JUST LABELS. Because MoSPI shifted the GDP base from 2011-12 to 2022-23 on 27 February 2026, growth rates and dollar-GDP levels published before and after that date are not directly comparable. A question comparing an old published figure with a new one is testing whether you know the series changed, not whether you can subtract.
ga-survey.timeTarget: IN THE EXAM: budget 12 seconds for a pure Survey-number question (recall or blank — do not deliberate at 0.25 negative) and up to 20 seconds for a concept or formula question such as GVA-to-GDP or the deflator, because those are actually solvable and the extra 8 seconds converts into a mark rather than a coin flip. Across a 40-question, 20-minute GA section, this topic should consume no more than about 90 seconds in total. IN PREPARATION: roughly 5 hours to build the four-block sheet and drill the two formulas until they are automatic, then 8 minutes of blank-paper recall daily and a 15-minute full rewrite weekly. Add a 5-minute monthly check of the volatile lines (repo rate, latest CPI print, inflation-target notification, IMF size ranking) — these are the only parts of the sheet that decay.
ga-survey.masteryCheck: Blank paper, 6-minute timer, no prompts. Write: (1) the Survey's tabling date, the ministry and department that prepare it, the CEA's name and the stated theme; (2) the growth chain 6.5 / 7.4 / 6.8-7.2 with the correct year against each and the label 'real'; (3) six supporting numbers with their reference periods attached (inflation 1.7% April-December, CAD 0.8% H1, FDI USD 81 bn, reserves 11 months, PFCE 61.5%, unemployment 3.2% PLFS 2023-24); (4) the four base years with the publishing body for each; (5) the GVA-to-GDP formula applied to a fresh set of numbers you invent, plus a deflator calculation from a nominal and a real growth rate. Then answer aloud, without looking: which index does the RBI target, which ministry publishes WPI, was the Survey tabled before or after the Budget, and is India currently the fourth or the sixth largest economy by nominal GDP per the IMF's April 2026 database. Mastery means all five written items and all four oral items correct inside 6 minutes, repeated on three separate days.
questionPatterns: Survey projection recall: 'The Economic Survey 2025-26 has projected India's real GDP growth for 2026-27 in the range of (a) 6.0% to 6.5% (b) 6.3% to 6.8% (c) 6.5% to 7.0% (d) 6.8% to 7.2% (e) 7.0% to 7.5%' — answer (d) 6.8% to 7.2%.

Authorship and identity: 'The Economic Survey is prepared by which of the following? (a) NITI Aayog (b) Reserve Bank of India (c) Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance (d) Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (e) Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance' — answer (c), under the Chief Economic Adviser.

Base-year update: 'MoSPI released the new series of national accounts in February 2026 with which base year? (a) 2011-12 (b) 2017-18 (c) 2020-21 (d) 2022-23 (e) 2024-25' — answer (d) 2022-23. Option (e) is planted because the new CPI series uses base year 2024.

Concept-with-formula: 'If GVA at basic prices is Rs 120 lakh crore, product taxes are Rs 18 lakh crore and product subsidies are Rs 6 lakh crore, GDP at market prices equals (a) Rs 96 lakh crore (b) Rs 108 lakh crore (c) Rs 126 lakh crore (d) Rs 132 lakh crore (e) Rs 144 lakh crore' — answer (d), since 120 + 18 − 6 = 132.

Institutional ownership: 'The Wholesale Price Index in India is compiled and released by (a) National Statistical Office, MoSPI (b) Reserve Bank of India (c) Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry (d) Central Statistics Office, Ministry of Finance (e) NITI Aayog' — answer (c).

Theme or one-liner: 'What is the stated theme of the Economic Survey 2025-26? (a) Viksit Bharat 2047 (b) Strategic Indispensability (c) Reform, Perform, Transform (d) Getting Back to Growth (e) Amrit Kaal Blueprint' — answer (b) Strategic Indispensability.

ga-survey.weightageNote: Zero questions in Prelims, which has no General Awareness section. In Mains, GA is 40 questions for 50 marks in 20 minutes and counts fully towards the final merit list. Economy items — Survey figures, GDP and inflation vocabulary, RBI policy rates — form one recurring cluster inside that 40, sitting alongside current affairs, banking awareness, government schemes, appointments and static GK; recent Mains analyses put current-affairs-based questions at roughly 60-65% of the section.
