ga-survey.websiteRef: indiabudget.gov.in/economicsurvey (the official full text and statistical appendix); prsindia.org (report summary of Economic Survey 2025-26, tabulated and short); mospi.gov.in (base-year revision FAQs and the new GDP, CPI and IIP series releases); rbi.org.in (MPC resolutions, repo rate history and the notified inflation-targeting framework — check this monthly, as the rate and the target period are the fastest-decaying facts on the sheet).

ga-intl-org.topicName: IMF, World Bank, ADB, AIIB, WTO
ga-intl-org.whatItIs: Five multilateral institutions that IBPS treats as a single static-GK block. Questions come in six predictable shapes: year established, headquarters city, current head and their nationality, number of members, flagship report, and India's position within the organisation. Because almost all of this is static, it is the cheapest sustained-return item in Mains GA — build the grid once, refresh the two or three volatile cells, and it holds for the whole cycle. The core content: the IMF and the World Bank both emerged from the July 1944 Bretton Woods conference and are both headquartered in Washington DC; the Asian Development Bank was founded in 1966 and sits in Manila; the World Trade Organization began on 1 January 1995 in Geneva as the successor to GATT; and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank began operations in Beijing in 2016. India is a founding member of the IMF, the World Bank and the ADB, is the second-largest shareholder in the AIIB, and is a founding member of the WTO.
ga-intl-org.coreMethod:
1. BUILD A 5 x 6 GRID ON ONE SHEET. Rows are the five organisations. Columns are: Established / HQ / Head and nationality / Members / Flagship report / India's position. Fill it column by column, not row by row — a column is one question family, and columns are far easier to reproduce than scattered facts.

2. COLUMN 1, ESTABLISHED. IMF: conceived at the Bretton Woods conference in July 1944, came into existence 27 December 1945, began financial operations 1 March 1947. World Bank: conceived at Bretton Woods 1944, IBRD began operations 25 June 1946. ADB: established 19 December 1966 with 31 members. WTO: established 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement, which was signed 15 April 1994; successor to GATT, which dated from 1948. AIIB: began operations in January 2016 with 57 founding members.

3. COLUMN 2, HEADQUARTERS. IMF Washington DC. World Bank Washington DC. ADB Manila, Philippines. AIIB Beijing, China. WTO Geneva, Switzerland.

4. COLUMN 3, HEAD AND NATIONALITY (verify these before the exam — this is the only genuinely volatile column). IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva of Bulgaria, second five-year term begun 1 October 2024; First Deputy Managing Director Dan Katz, effective 6 October 2025. World Bank President Ajay Banga, in office since 2 June 2023. ADB President Masato Kanda of Japan, the eleventh president, who took office 24 February 2025 to complete his predecessor's unexpired term ending 23 November 2026; he was the sole nominee for re-election, with Board of Governors voting running 2 July to 31 August 2026, so check the outcome. AIIB President Zou Jiayi of China, who took office 16 January 2026 succeeding founding president Jin Liqun. WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala of Nigeria, the first woman and first African to hold the post, serving a second term.

5. COLUMN 4, MEMBERS. IMF 191 (Liechtenstein became the 191st in October 2024). World Bank: IBRD 189 and IDA 175 — the World Bank Group has five institutions, IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID, each with its own membership. ADB 69 members, of which 50 are regional and 19 non-regional; Israel joined as the 69th. AIIB over 111 approved members, comprising 53 regional and 58 non-regional. WTO 166 members, and it decides by consensus.

6. COLUMN 5, FLAGSHIP REPORTS. IMF: World Economic Outlook, Global Financial Stability Report, Fiscal Monitor. World Bank: World Development Report, Global Economic Prospects (January and June), and Business Ready or B-READY, which replaced the discontinued Doing Business report. ADB: Asian Development Outlook. AIIB: Asian Infrastructure Finance. WTO: World Trade Report and the Trade Policy Review.

7. COLUMN 6, INDIA'S POSITION. IMF: quota 2.75%, voting power 2.63%. World Bank: founding member, one of the largest IDA and IBRD borrowers historically. ADB: founding member; shareholding — Japan and the United States are joint largest at about 12.756% each, China about 6.429%, India about 6.317%, making India the third-largest shareholder. AIIB: China is the largest shareholder at about 26.54% of votes and India is second at about 7.58%, ahead of Russia and Germany. WTO: founding member from 1 January 1995.

8. ADD THE SDR CARD (asked separately and often). The IMF's Special Drawing Right is valued on a basket of five currencies: US dollar 43.38%, euro 29.31%, Chinese renminbi 12.28%, Japanese yen 7.59%, pound sterling 7.44%. The basket is reviewed every five years. The rupee is NOT in it.

9. ADD THE ONE LIVE EVENT. The WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference, MC14, was held in Yaoundé, Cameroon from 26 to 30 March 2026, chaired by Cameroon's trade minister, and closed WITHOUT an overall ministerial declaration and without agreement on its core priorities; work on a 'Yaoundé Package' continued in Geneva. MC13 was in Abu Dhabi in February 2024. Ministerial conferences meet at least once every two years and are the WTO's top decision-making body.

10. DRILL PROTOCOL. Reproduce one full COLUMN from blank paper daily — six days covers the grid twice a week. Once a week, reproduce the whole grid in 5 minutes. Once a month, re-verify only Column 3 against the organisations' own websites, since leadership is the one thing that moves.

11. EXAM PROTOCOL. These are 8-to-10-second questions. If the cell does not surface immediately, it is not going to; blank it and move, because 0.25 negative marking makes a five-way guess negative in expectation.
tricks: HEADQUARTERS COLLAPSE FROM FIVE FACTS TO THREE GROUPS. The two Bretton Woods twins share Washington DC. The two Asia-focused banks split by their lead sponsor: ADB in Manila (1966, Japan and the US as joint largest shareholders) and AIIB in Beijing (2016, China-led). WTO stands alone in Geneva. Three chunks instead of five entries, and the sponsor logic makes each one recoverable rather than merely memorised.

THE DATE LADDER ANSWERS EVERY 'OLDEST / NEWEST / WHICH CAME FIRST' QUESTION IN ONE GLANCE: 1944-45 IMF, 1946 IBRD operations, 1966 ADB, 1995 WTO, 2016 AIIB. Learn the five-item ordered list as a single string and you never have to compare pairs of dates under time pressure.

THE 'OUTLOOK' SPLIT ASSIGNS REPORTS TO OWNERS IN UNDER FIVE SECONDS. World Economic Outlook is the IMF. Asian Development Outlook is the ADB. Global Economic Prospects and World Development Report are the World Bank. World Trade Report is the WTO. Asian Infrastructure Finance is the AIIB. The adjective in front of the word tells you the organisation — 'World Economic' to the world's monetary fund, 'Asian Development' to the Asian development bank.

WRITE INDIA'S RANKS AS A SINGLE COLUMN, NOT AS SCATTERED FACTS. AIIB: India is second at about 7.58% of votes, behind China's 26.54%. ADB: India is third at about 6.317%, behind Japan and the US at about 12.756% each. IMF: India's quota is 2.75% and voting power 2.63%. Reading them down one column makes the pattern — second, third, and a small single-digit quota — memorable in a way that three isolated facts never are.

NATIONALITY IS ASKED AS OFTEN AS NAME, SO STORE THEM AS PAIRS. Georgieva/Bulgaria for the IMF, Kanda/Japan for the ADB, Zou Jiayi/China for the AIIB, Okonjo-Iweala/Nigeria for the WTO. A question reading 'the head of which organisation is a national of Nigeria' is a different retrieval path from 'who heads the WTO', and only the paired encoding serves both.

USE MEMBERSHIP SIZE ORDER AS A CROSS-CHECK ON A NUMBER YOU HALF-REMEMBER: IMF 191 > IBRD 189 > IDA 175 > WTO 166 > AIIB 111 > ADB 69. If you recall 'about 110' for a body and the stem is about the ADB, the ordering tells you immediately that you have pulled the AIIB row. This validates a recalled figure; it does not license picking one you never learned.
traps: AIIB IS BEIJING; THE BRICS NEW DEVELOPMENT BANK IS SHANGHAI. Two multilateral banks, two Chinese cities, and options routinely offer both. Anchor it as 'AIIB, Asia, Beijing the capital' versus 'NDB, BRICS, Shanghai'.

GATT WAS AN AGREEMENT, NOT AN ORGANISATION, AND THE WTO DATES FROM 1995. GATT dates from 1948; the WTO was established on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement, which was itself signed on 15 April 1994. Three defensible-looking years — 1948, 1994, 1995 — appear together as options. Read whether the stem says 'established', 'agreement signed' or 'predecessor'.

'WORLD BANK' AND 'WORLD BANK GROUP' HAVE DIFFERENT MEMBERSHIPS, AND NEITHER IS 191. IBRD has 189 members and IDA has 175; the Group comprises five institutions (IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA, ICSID) each with its own count. 191 is the IMF's number. Candidates who learned 'the Bretton Woods twins' as interchangeable mark 191 for both and lose the mark.

THE IMF HAS THREE DEFENSIBLE FOUNDING DATES AND THE STEM PICKS ONE. Conceived at Bretton Woods in July 1944; came into existence 27 December 1945; began financial operations 1 March 1947. If the stem says 'came into existence' the answer is 1945, not 1944. Reading the verb is the whole question.

DOING BUSINESS IS DEAD; B-READY IS THE SUCCESSOR. The World Bank discontinued the Doing Business report in 2021 and replaced it with Business Ready (B-READY). Quoting India's old 'ease of doing business rank' is quoting a discontinued series, and an option offering Doing Business as a current World Bank flagship is a deliberate trap on candidates using pre-2022 material.

THE ADB PRESIDENCY IS MID-CYCLE IN 2026. Masato Kanda took office on 24 February 2025 to complete his predecessor's unexpired term, which ENDS 23 November 2026 — before your 27 December Mains. He stood as sole nominee for re-election with voting from 2 July to 31 August 2026. Do not carry a leadership answer into December without re-checking adb.org; the same caution applies to the IMF's and World Bank's chief-economist posts, both of which changed hands in mid-2026.

AIIB'S COUNT IS OF 'APPROVED MEMBERS', AND ITS FOUNDING COUNT WAS DIFFERENT. AIIB reports over 111 approved members (53 regional, 58 non-regional), but it began operations in 2016 with 57 founding members. Stems distinguish 'founding members', 'approved members' and 'members' and the three numbers are 57, 111 and a figure the organisation itself qualifies. Match the adjective in the stem.

MC14 PRODUCED NO MINISTERIAL DECLARATION. The WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference in Yaoundé, Cameroon (26-30 March 2026) closed without an overall declaration and without agreement on its core priorities. An option claiming a 'Yaoundé Declaration was adopted' is wrong; work on a Yaoundé Package continued afterwards in Geneva. Venue-and-year questions and outcome questions have different answers here.
ga-intl-org.timeTarget: IN THE EXAM: 8-10 seconds per question. These are single-cell lookups from a grid you have reproduced dozens of times; if the cell does not surface within 10 seconds it will not surface at all, so blank it — a five-way guess at 0.25 negative marking loses marks in expectation. Across a 20-minute, 40-question GA section, the whole international-organisations cluster should cost you under 60 seconds and should be among the first questions you clear, banking time for the Reasoning and Quant sections. IN PREPARATION: about 4 hours to build the 5 x 6 grid and first-memorise it, then roughly 6 minutes daily reproducing one column and 5 minutes weekly reproducing the whole grid. Add a 10-minute monthly check of the leadership column only. Because five of the six columns are static, this topic decays more slowly than any other GA item — the maintenance cost after month one is genuinely small.
ga-intl-org.masteryCheck: Draw an empty 5 x 6 grid — five organisations down, six columns across (Established, HQ, Head and nationality, Members, Flagship report, India's position) — and fill every one of the 30 cells from memory in 5 minutes with no prompts. Then answer four cross-cutting questions aloud without looking: which two of the five share a headquarters city and why; list the five organisations in order of founding; name the flagship report of each; and state India's shareholder rank in the AIIB and in the ADB. Finally, check your three most volatile cells — the ADB, AIIB and IMF leadership rows — against adb.org, aiib.org and imf.org, and correct any drift. Mastery means 28 of 30 cells correct inside 5 minutes on three separate days, with the four cross-cutting answers instant. If the grid takes more than 5 minutes, you are recalling facts one at a time rather than reproducing a structure, and it will not survive a 30-second-per-question clock.
questionPatterns: Headquarters identification: 'The headquarters of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is located in (a) Shanghai (b) Manila (c) Beijing (d) Singapore (e) Hong Kong' — answer (c) Beijing. Shanghai is planted because it is the headquarters of the BRICS New Development Bank.

Leadership and nationality: 'Who is the Director-General of the World Trade Organization? (a) Kristalina Georgieva (b) Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (c) Ajay Banga (d) Masato Kanda (e) Zou Jiayi' — answer (b), the first woman and first African to hold the post. The distractors are precisely the heads of the other four organisations in this topic.

Membership count: 'The Asian Development Bank currently has how many members? (a) 49 (b) 57 (c) 68 (d) 69 (e) 111' — answer (d) 69, of which 50 are regional and 19 non-regional. Option (b) is AIIB's founding count and (e) is AIIB's current approved-member count.

Report ownership: 'The Global Economic Prospects report is published by (a) International Monetary Fund (b) World Bank (c) World Trade Organization (d) Asian Development Bank (e) United Nations Conference on Trade and Development' — answer (b) World Bank, released each January and June.

India's standing: 'India is the ______ largest shareholder of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank. (a) first (b) second (c) third (d) fourth (e) fifth' — answer (b) second, with about 7.58% of voting shares, behind China's 26.54%.

Founding year with near-miss options: 'The World Trade Organization came into existence on (a) 1 January 1948 (b) 15 April 1994 (c) 1 January 1995 (d) 1 January 1996 (e) 27 December 1945' — answer (c). Option (a) is GATT, (b) is the date the Marrakesh Agreement was signed, and (e) is the IMF's date.
ga-intl-org.searchQuery: IMF World Bank ADB AIIB WTO headquarters established year current head number of members India shareholding official about pages
ga-intl-org.aiPrompt: Act as an IBPS Clerk Mains General Awareness question setter. Generate 20 multiple-choice questions on five international organisations: the IMF, the World Bank Group, the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the World Trade Organization. STRICT FORMAT RULES: every question must have EXACTLY FIVE options labelled (a), (b), (c), (d), (e) — IBPS papers always use five options, never four. Distribute as: 4 on headquarters, 4 on year of establishment, 4 on current heads and their nationalities, 3 on membership numbers, 3 on flagship reports, and 2 on India's position or shareholding. Design the distractors from within this same set of five organisations rather than from unrelated bodies — for example, offer Shanghai against Beijing, offer 189 and 191 against each other, and offer 1948, 1994 and 1995 together for the WTO. Print the 20 questions first with no answers. Then print an answer key that gives, for each question, the correct option letter plus one sentence of justification naming the official source page (imf.org, worldbank.org, adb.org, aiib.org or wto.org). Finally, add a short list flagging which of your 20 answers are time-sensitive and should be re-verified before December 2026 — leadership appointments and membership counts in particular. Do not invent any figure or name; skip a question rather than guess.
ga-intl-org.blockPlan: SETUP PHASE (three days): two 2-hour sessions in your GA slot to build the 5 x 6 grid directly from the five organisations' own 'about us' pages, filling it column by column. MAINTENANCE PHASE (February to September): 6 minutes at the end of your daily 4 hours reproducing one column from blank paper — six days covers the grid twice a week — plus a 5-minute whole-grid reproduction on your weekly review day. Once a month, spend 10 minutes re-verifying only the leadership column, since that is the one part that moves; put a specific reminder in early September to check the ADB presidency outcome, as the Board of Governors voting ran 2 July to 31 August 2026. INTENSIVE PHASE (mid-October to 27 December, after Prelims): fold into a 60-minute daily GA block, rotating with ga-budget and ga-survey so each is touched twice a week, plus a 40-question mixed GA mock every Sunday under a 20-minute clock — and in those mocks, deliberately answer the international-organisation questions FIRST, because clearing them in under 10 seconds each is what creates the time buffer for the harder current-affairs items. Spend no time on this topic in the fortnight before the 10-11 October Prelims; Prelims has no GA section.
ga-intl-org.weightageNote: Zero questions in Prelims, which has no General Awareness section at all. In Mains, GA is 40 questions for 50 marks in 20 minutes and counts in full towards the final merit list. International organisations sit within the static and banking-awareness portion of that section rather than the current-affairs portion, which recent Mains analyses put at roughly 60-65% of the paper — so this cluster is a smaller but far more stable slice. Its real value is the return per hour rather than the raw count: five of the six columns in the grid do not change between now and December, so four hours of setup plus about 30 minutes a week protects those marks for the entire cycle, whereas the current-affairs bulk of GA needs continuous fresh input right up to exam day.
ga-intl-org.bookRef: Lucent's General Knowledge (book named without a chapter reference, since chapter titles vary across editions) — usable for the static skeleton of these organisations, but every membership count, leadership name and report title must be cross-checked against the official websites below, because printed general-knowledge compendia lag leadership changes by a year or more.
ga-intl-org.websiteRef: imf.org ('IMF at a Glance' factsheet, Senior Officials, and the Members' Quotas and Voting Power page); worldbank.org (Leadership and Member Countries pages, and the Business Ready section); adb.org ('Who We Are' and 'About ADB'); aiib.org (Membership Status and Leadership pages); wto.org ('Who we are' and the Members and Observers page, plus the MC14 section). These five official pages are the only sources that should settle a disputed figure — coaching PDFs and aggregator sites carry stale leadership and membership numbers.

ga-payments.topicName: Payment Systems — NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI, AEPS
ga-payments.whatItIs: The five retail and wholesale money-movement rails used in India, and the rules that separate them. Examiners test three things: WHO operates each system (the Reserve Bank of India runs RTGS and NEFT; the National Payments Corporation of India runs IMPS, UPI, AEPS, NACH, RuPay, Bharat BillPay and FASTag), HOW each settles (real-time and one-by-one, or in timed batches), and WHAT the amount limits and identifiers are. This is a pure recall topic with no reasoning, which makes it fast marks in a 40-question, 20-minute General Awareness section — but the numbers change by circular, so what you memorise must be current. All figures below were verified in 2026 and should be re-checked in the fortnight before the Mains on 27 December 2026.
ga-payments.coreMethod:
1. LEARN THE OWNERSHIP SPLIT FIRST, because it is the most frequently asked single fact. RBI owns and operates RTGS and NEFT. NPCI operates IMPS, UPI, AEPS, NACH, RuPay, BBPS/Bharat BillPay, NETC FASTag and Cheque Truncation-related retail services. NPCI was incorporated in 2008 as a not-for-profit company promoted by the RBI and the Indian Banks' Association under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
2. LEARN THE SETTLEMENT MECHANISM, which the acronyms encode. RTGS = Real Time Gross Settlement: each instruction settles individually and immediately, with no netting. NEFT = National Electronic Funds Transfer: deferred NET settlement, so instructions are pooled and settled in batches — currently 48 half-hourly batches a day, at 00:00, 00:30, 01:00 and so on through 23:30. Both have been available 24x7x365: NEFT since 16 December 2019, RTGS since 14 December 2020.
3. LEARN THE LIMITS AS A LADDER OF PER-TRANSACTION CEILINGS, with RTGS deliberately placed outside it.
   - UPI Lite: Rs 1,000 per transaction; on-device wallet balance capped at Rs 5,000; no UPI PIN required for a payment.
   - AEPS: Rs 10,000 per transaction; NPCI also caps cumulative inward-plus-outward fund transfer at Rs 50,000 per account per month.
   - UPI 123Pay (feature phones, no internet): Rs 10,000 per transaction.
   - UPI (normal): Rs 1 lakh per transaction by default; up to Rs 5 lakh per transaction in specified categories such as capital markets, insurance, education and healthcare.
   - IMPS: Rs 5 lakh per transaction (raised from Rs 2 lakh in 2021).
   - RTGS: MINIMUM Rs 2 lakh per customer transaction, with NO maximum prescribed by the RBI. It is the only one of the five with a floor rather than a ceiling.
   - NEFT: no minimum and no maximum prescribed by the RBI; however, cash-based walk-in remittances are capped at Rs 50,000 per transaction.
   Banks may impose tighter limits than any of these.
4. LEARN THE IDENTIFIERS. NEFT and RTGS use the beneficiary's account number plus the 11-character IFSC. IMPS can use account number plus IFSC, OR mobile number plus MMID (a 7-digit Mobile Money Identifier). UPI uses a Virtual Payment Address (a UPI ID such as name@bank) or a mobile number or a QR code, and requires a UPI PIN. AEPS uses only the Aadhaar number, the bank's IIN, and a biometric (fingerprint or iris) — no card, no PIN, no signature, no cheque.
5. LEARN AEPS AS THE FINANCIAL-INCLUSION RAIL. It is delivered through Business Correspondents at micro-ATMs and supports cash withdrawal, cash deposit, balance enquiry, mini statement, Aadhaar-to-Aadhaar fund transfer, eKYC and best-finger detection.
6. LEARN THE CHARGES POSITION. The RBI waived its own processing and time-varying charges on RTGS and NEFT from 1 July 2019, and from 1 January 2020 directed banks not to levy charges on savings account holders for online NEFT transactions.
7. KEEP TWO CURRENT-AFFAIRS ITEMS READY. UPI is built on the IMPS infrastructure and was launched by NPCI in 2016. NPCI's proposed 30% market-share cap on third-party UPI application providers has been deferred to 31 December 2026, so it is live current affairs during this exam cycle.
tricks: Decode the acronym instead of memorising the behaviour. 'Gross' in RTGS means one-by-one with no netting, which is why it is instant; 'Net' in NEFT's deferred net settlement means pooled, which is why it is batched. An examiner asking 'which of these settles on a deferred net basis' is answerable from the expansion alone.

Fix the ownership with one sentence: 'The RBI runs the two that need an IFSC and a bank branch; NPCI runs everything you can do from a phone.' RTGS and NEFT are RBI; IMPS, UPI, AEPS are NPCI. This resolves the most commonly asked question type in a second.

Store RTGS separately from the limits ladder because it is the exception — it is the only system with a MINIMUM. Trying to remember 'RTGS = 2 lakh' as a ceiling is the single most reliable way to lose this mark; encode it as 'RTGS starts at 2 lakh'.

Link each system to its unique identifier and answer identifier questions without recalling anything else: MMID belongs to IMPS and nothing else; VPA belongs to UPI and nothing else; a biometric belongs to AEPS and nothing else; IFSC belongs to NEFT, RTGS and IMPS.

Memorise the batch count as '48 half-hourly batches, on the hour and the half hour'. Questions frequently ask for the number of NEFT settlement batches per day, and 48 follows immediately from 24 x 2 if you have stored the interval rather than the count.
traps: Believing RTGS has a maximum limit. The RBI prescribes a minimum of Rs 2 lakh per customer transaction and no upper ceiling; individual banks may set their own channel-wise caps, but that is a bank rule, not an RBI rule. Options offering 'Rs 10 lakh' or 'Rs 25 lakh' as the RTGS maximum are testing exactly this.

Believing NEFT has a minimum. It does not. The Rs 50,000 figure attached to NEFT applies only to CASH-BASED walk-in remittances, not to account-to-account transfers, and options exploit this by presenting Rs 50,000 as a general NEFT ceiling.

Describing NEFT as instantaneous. It is batch-settled; credit reaches the beneficiary within a defined window after the batch in which the instruction settles. A question contrasting 'real-time' with 'batch' is asking you to separate RTGS from NEFT.
Assigning UPI or IMPS to the RBI. Both are NPCI products. Equally, assigning RTGS to NPCI. The ownership split is asked directly and in 'which of the following is NOT operated by NPCI' form.
Saying AEPS requires a debit card or a PIN. It requires an Aadhaar number, the issuing bank's IIN and a biometric. Options mentioning a card, a PIN or a cheque are wrong by construction.

Quoting the UPI limit as a flat Rs 1 lakh. Rs 1 lakh is the default; specified categories including capital markets, insurance, education and healthcare permit up to Rs 5 lakh per transaction. A question naming one of those categories is testing the exception.
Confusing UPI Lite's two numbers. Rs 1,000 is the per-transaction cap; Rs 5,000 is the maximum balance the on-device wallet may hold. Both appear as options in the same question.
ga-payments.timeTarget: GA in Mains is 40 questions in 20 minutes, an average of 30 seconds per question, and banking-awareness recall questions should be answered well inside that. A direct ownership or identifier question: 10-15 seconds. A limit question: 15-20 seconds. A statement-based 'which of the following is/are correct' question with three or four statements: 35-45 seconds. If a payments question takes you longer than 45 seconds, the fact is not memorised and no amount of thinking will produce it — mark it and move, since 0.25 is deducted for a wrong answer.
ga-payments.masteryCheck: You have mastered this when you can fill a blank five-column table — system, operator, settlement type, minimum, maximum — for RTGS, NEFT, IMPS, UPI and AEPS from memory in under three minutes with no errors. Second check: answer these four instantly and correctly — the number of NEFT settlement batches in a day (48); the identifier unique to IMPS (MMID); whether NEFT has a minimum (no); whether RTGS has a maximum set by the RBI (no). Third check: score 9 or better on 10 mixed payment-system questions from a recent question bank in under 5 minutes.
questionPatterns: Ownership: 'Which of the following payment systems is NOT operated by the National Payments Corporation of India?' with RTGS as the correct answer among IMPS, UPI, AEPS and NACH.
Limit: 'What is the minimum amount that can be remitted through RTGS as prescribed by the RBI?' — Rs 2 lakh, with Rs 1 lakh, Rs 5 lakh, Rs 10 lakh and 'no minimum' as the other five options.

Settlement mechanism: 'NEFT operates on which basis?' — deferred net settlement in half-hourly batches, contrasted with real-time gross settlement, continuous netting, end-of-day settlement and T+1 settlement.
Identifier: 'MMID, used to route an IMPS transfer against a mobile number, consists of how many digits?' — 7.

AEPS specifics: 'Which of the following is NOT a service available under AEPS?' with 'cheque book request' or 'opening a fixed deposit' as the correct answer among cash withdrawal, balance enquiry, mini statement and Aadhaar-to-Aadhaar fund transfer.

Multi-statement: 'Consider the following about UPI Lite: (i) it works without a UPI PIN; (ii) the per-transaction limit is Rs 1,000; (iii) the maximum wallet balance is Rs 5,000. Which are correct?' — all three, presented among five combinations.
Current affairs: 'NPCI has deferred the implementation of the 30% market-share cap on third-party UPI apps to which date?' — 31 December 2026.
ga-payments.searchQuery: IBPS Clerk mains banking awareness NEFT RTGS IMPS UPI AEPS limits operator questions 2026
ga-payments.aiPrompt: Act as an IBPS Clerk 2026 General Awareness coach for the banking-awareness section. Generate 20 multiple-choice questions on Indian payment systems (NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI, UPI Lite, UPI 123Pay, AEPS, NACH, BBPS), each with EXACTLY FIVE options labelled (a) to (e). Cover: operator (RBI versus NPCI), settlement mechanism, minimum and maximum limits, identifiers (IFSC, MMID, VPA, Aadhaar plus IIN), launch years, and services available. Include at least 4 statement-based questions of the form 'which of the following statements is/are correct' with five combination options. Deliberately include distractors that reflect these real confusions: that RTGS has a maximum, that NEFT has a minimum, that UPI is operated by the RBI, that AEPS needs a debit card or PIN, and that the UPI limit is a flat Rs 1 lakh with no category exceptions. Provide an answer key with a one-line justification for each answer and, where a figure is set by circular, state that the figure should be re-verified close to the exam date because NPCI and RBI revise these. Do not invent any figure you are unsure of — say 'verify' instead.
ga-payments.blockPlan: A 75-minute block, best done as a build-and-recite exercise rather than reading. Minutes 0-25: build a single five-column table by hand — system, operator, settlement type, minimum, maximum — for RTGS, NEFT, IMPS, UPI, UPI Lite, UPI 123Pay and AEPS, sourcing every number from rbi.org.in or npci.org.in rather than from a coaching PDF. Minutes 25-40: build a second, smaller table of identifiers and add the launch years (NEFT 2005, IMPS 2010, UPI 2016, AEPS via NPCI, RTGS 2004). Minutes 40-55: close both tables and rewrite them from memory; mark every cell you missed. Minutes 55-70: attempt 20 mixed questions from a current question bank and log every wrong answer against the specific cell of the table that failed. Minutes 70-75: write the two current-affairs items (24x7 dates, the 30% UPI market-cap deferral to 31 December 2026) on a revision card. Re-recite the table for 10 minutes every week until Mains, and re-verify the limit figures in the fortnight before 27 December 2026.
ga-payments.weightageNote: This topic carries no weight in Prelims, where there is no General Awareness section. In Mains, General Awareness is 40 questions for 50 marks in 20 minutes, and banking and financial awareness is the largest recognisable block within it. Payment systems is a recurring sub-area of that block, typically worth a small number of direct questions per paper. Its value lies in cost-effectiveness rather than volume: the entire topic is one table, it is asked as pure recall, and marks come at roughly 15 seconds each. Confidence is marked medium only because NPCI and RBI revise the limit figures by circular, so the numbers must be re-verified before the exam.
ga-payments.websiteRef: https://www.rbi.org.in (RBI FAQs on NEFT and RTGS, and the Payment and Settlement Systems pages) and https://www.npci.org.in (product pages and circulars for IMPS, UPI, UPI Lite, UPI 123Pay and AEPS)

ga-accounts.topicName: Account Types — Savings, Current, FD, RD, NRI
ga-accounts.whatItIs: The deposit products a bank offers and the rules that distinguish them: who may open each, whether interest is paid, what restrictions apply, how the interest is taxed, and how much of the money is insured. It splits into three groups. DEMAND deposits — savings and current — are payable on demand. TERM deposits — fixed and recurring — are locked for a chosen period at a fixed rate. NRI deposits — NRE, NRO and FCNR(B) — are governed by FEMA and differ chiefly in currency, taxability and repatriability. Examiners ask this as pure recall, usually as a difference question ('which of the following is true of a current account') or a multi-statement question. Figures verified in 2026; the tax thresholds in particular should be re-checked before the Mains on 27 December 2026.
ga-accounts.coreMethod:
1. SAVINGS ACCOUNT. For individuals and certain non-trading entities; not for business or trading purposes. Interest is calculated on the DAILY closing balance (mandatory since 1 April 2010) and credited at quarterly or shorter intervals. The rate has been deregulated since October 2011, so each bank sets its own. Banks may restrict the number of free withdrawals and may require a minimum balance.
2. CURRENT ACCOUNT. For businesses, firms and companies. NO interest is payable. Unlimited transactions, overdraft facility available, cheque-book and other business services. The trade-off is simple: liquidity and volume instead of interest.
3. BSBDA (Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account). A zero-balance savings account that must be offered free of charge with no minimum balance requirement, a free RuPay ATM-cum-debit card, and a minimum of four withdrawals per month at no charge. A BSBDA holder may not hold any other savings account in the same bank. The related SMALL ACCOUNT, for people lacking officially valid KYC documents, is subject to a balance ceiling of Rs 50,000, annual credits of Rs 1 lakh, and monthly withdrawals of Rs 10,000, and is normally valid for 12 months, extendable.
4. FIXED DEPOSIT (FD). A lump sum locked for a chosen tenor, commonly from 7 days up to 10 years, at a rate fixed at the time of booking. Premature withdrawal usually attracts a penalty and a lower applicable rate. Loans or overdrafts are typically available against the deposit. A TAX-SAVER FD has a 5-year lock-in, qualifies for deduction under Section 80C up to Rs 1.5 lakh, and permits neither premature withdrawal nor a loan against it.
5. RECURRING DEPOSIT (RD). A fixed instalment paid every month for a chosen period, earning the same order of interest as an FD. It suits salaried savers building a corpus rather than deploying one.
6. TAX POSITION. Interest on FDs and RDs is fully taxable. Under Section 194A, banks deduct TDS at 10% once the interest paid in a financial year exceeds Rs 50,000 for a general depositor or Rs 1 lakh for a senior citizen (thresholds effective from FY 2025-26); the rate becomes 20% if PAN is not furnished. Form 15G (for those below 60) or Form 15H (for senior citizens) may be submitted to avoid deduction where total income is below the taxable limit. TDS is not deducted on savings account interest, though that interest is still taxable.
7. NRI ACCOUNTS — THREE, DISTINGUISHED BY CURRENCY, TAX AND REPATRIATION.
   - NRE (Non-Resident External): held in Indian rupees, funded from income earned ABROAD. Interest is exempt from Indian income tax. Principal and interest are fully repatriable. The depositor bears the rupee exchange-rate risk.
   - NRO (Non-Resident Ordinary): held in Indian rupees, for income earned IN India such as rent, dividends and pension. Interest is taxable in India. Repatriation is permitted up to USD 1 million per financial year, subject to tax compliance and the filing of Forms 15CA and 15CB.
   - FCNR(B) (Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Banks)): a TERM DEPOSIT ONLY, held in a permitted foreign currency, with a tenor of 1 year to 5 years. Interest is exempt from Indian income tax and the deposit is fully repatriable. Because it is denominated in foreign currency, the depositor carries no rupee exchange risk.
8. DEPOSIT INSURANCE. The DICGC insures deposits up to Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank, covering principal plus interest, aggregated across all branches of that bank for deposits held in the same right and capacity. Savings, current, fixed and recurring deposits are covered, as are NRE, NRO and FCNR(B) deposits held with an insured bank in India. Excluded are deposits of foreign governments, deposits of the Central and State Governments, inter-bank deposits, and any amount due on a deposit received outside India.
9. NOMINATION. Under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, with the relevant provisions in force from 1 November 2025, a depositor may nominate up to FOUR persons for a deposit account or a locker, either successively (in order of priority) or simultaneously (with specified shares totalling 100%).
10. DORMANCY AND UNCLAIMED DEPOSITS. An account with no customer-induced transaction for two years is classified as inoperative. Deposits unclaimed for ten years are transferred to the RBI's Depositor Education and Awareness (DEA) Fund, and can be searched through the RBI's UDGAM portal.
tricks: Sort every account question by asking one question first: is this a DEMAND deposit or a TERM deposit? Savings and current are demand; FD and RD are term. Almost every 'which of the following' option about premature withdrawal, penalties or fixed tenors resolves the moment you place the product in the right bucket.

Fix the NRI trio with a three-word tag each: NRE is 'foreign money, rupee account, tax-free'; NRO is 'Indian money, rupee account, taxable'; FCNR(B) is 'foreign currency, term deposit only, tax-free'. Every NRI question in this exam is answerable from those three tags plus the USD 1 million NRO repatriation cap.

Remember that current accounts pay NO interest as a rule with no threshold attached to it. Options that offer '2% on current accounts' or 'interest above a balance of Rs 1 lakh' are wrong by construction, which lets you eliminate before reading the rest.

Store the two TDS thresholds as a pair — Rs 50,000 general and Rs 1 lakh senior citizen — because IBPS asks them together and the senior-citizen figure is exactly double. Attach '10% with PAN, 20% without' to the same card.

Encode the DICGC cover as 'Rs 5 lakh, per depositor, per bank, principal plus interest'. Each of those four phrases is separately tested: options will vary the amount, or say 'per account' instead of 'per depositor', or 'per branch' instead of 'per bank', or 'principal only'.
traps: Thinking DICGC cover is per account or per branch. It is per depositor per bank, with all branches of that bank aggregated. Someone with four accounts at one bank is covered to Rs 5 lakh in total, not Rs 20 lakh.
Thinking DICGC covers only the principal. It covers principal PLUS interest, subject to the Rs 5 lakh ceiling.
Assuming FCNR(B) can be a savings account. It is a TERM DEPOSIT ONLY, with a tenor of 1 to 5 years. NRE and NRO can each be savings, current, recurring or fixed; FCNR(B) cannot.

Swapping NRE and NRO on taxability. NRE interest is tax-free in India; NRO interest is taxable. The mnemonic that fails people is the one based on the letters, so anchor instead on the source of the money: money earned in India is taxed in India.
Believing the NRO repatriation limit is per calendar year or per transaction. It is USD 1 million per FINANCIAL YEAR, and it requires tax compliance with Forms 15CA and 15CB.

Applying the old TDS threshold of Rs 40,000. From FY 2025-26 it is Rs 50,000 for general depositors and Rs 1 lakh for senior citizens under Section 194A. Papers set after April 2025 test the revised figures.

Assuming a tax-saver FD behaves like an ordinary FD. It has a compulsory 5-year lock-in, cannot be broken prematurely, and no loan can be taken against it — the exact opposite of the ordinary FD's flexibility.

Stating that only one nominee is permitted per deposit account. Since 1 November 2025 up to four nominees are permitted, either successively or simultaneously — a change recent enough to be a live current-affairs question in this cycle.
Confusing the two-year dormancy trigger with the ten-year transfer to the DEA Fund. Two years makes an account inoperative; ten years sends the money to the DEA Fund.
ga-accounts.timeTarget: A direct single-fact question (DICGC limit, current account interest, FCNR tenor): 10-15 seconds. An NRE-versus-NRO comparison question: 20-25 seconds. A multi-statement question with three or four statements and five combination options: 40-50 seconds. Within the 20-minute, 40-question GA section this topic should be net positive on time, buying seconds for the current-affairs questions that need thought. If a question here runs past 45 seconds, leave it blank rather than risk the 0.25 deduction.
ga-accounts.masteryCheck: You have mastered this when you can produce, from a blank page in under four minutes, a comparison table of NRE, NRO and FCNR(B) across five columns — currency, source of funds, account types permitted, taxability of interest, repatriability — with no errors. Second check: state these five instantly and correctly — the DICGC limit and its unit of application (Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank, principal plus interest); the FCNR(B) tenor range (1 to 5 years); the Section 194A TDS threshold for a senior citizen (Rs 1 lakh); the tax-saver FD lock-in (5 years); the maximum number of nominees permitted for a deposit account since 1 November 2025 (four). Third check: 10 mixed account-type questions, 9 correct, in 5 minutes.
questionPatterns: Direct fact: 'Deposits with a commercial bank in India are insured by the DICGC up to what amount?' — Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank including interest, offered against Rs 1 lakh, Rs 2 lakh, Rs 10 lakh and 'the full amount'.

Difference question: 'Which of the following is true of a current account?' with 'no interest is payable on the balance' correct among options claiming quarterly interest, a Rs 10,000 minimum balance mandated by the RBI, restricted withdrawals, and a compulsory lock-in.
NRI comparison: 'Interest earned on which of the following accounts is taxable in India?' — the NRO account, offered alongside NRE savings, NRE fixed deposit, FCNR(B) and 'none of these'.
Tenor: 'What is the permissible maturity period for an FCNR(B) deposit?' — not less than 1 year and not more than 5 years.
Tax: 'From which financial year did the TDS threshold on bank interest for senior citizens under Section 194A rise to Rs 1 lakh?' — FY 2025-26.

Multi-statement: 'Consider the following about a Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account: (i) no minimum balance is required; (ii) a minimum of four withdrawals per month must be free; (iii) the holder may simultaneously hold another savings account in the same bank. Which are correct?' — (i) and (ii) only, presented among five combinations.
Current affairs: 'Under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, how many nominees may a depositor appoint for a bank deposit account?' — up to four.
ga-accounts.searchQuery: IBPS Clerk mains banking awareness savings current fixed recurring NRE NRO FCNR DICGC questions 2026
ga-accounts.aiPrompt: Act as an IBPS Clerk 2026 General Awareness coach for the banking-awareness section. Produce 20 multiple-choice questions on Indian bank deposit account types, each with EXACTLY FIVE options labelled (a) to (e). Cover savings accounts, current accounts, BSBDA and small accounts, fixed deposits including tax-saver FDs, recurring deposits, and the NRI trio of NRE, NRO and FCNR(B), plus DICGC deposit insurance, Section 194A TDS thresholds, nomination rules, and the inoperative-account and DEA Fund rules. Include at least 5 statement-based questions with five combination options. Deliberately build distractors around these real confusions: DICGC cover being per account or per branch rather than per depositor per bank; DICGC covering principal only; FCNR(B) being available as a savings account; NRE interest being taxable; the NRO repatriation cap being per calendar year; the TDS threshold still being Rs 40,000; and only one nominee being permitted. Give an answer key with a one-line justification for each. For any figure set by statute, circular or the annual Finance Act, add a note telling me to re-verify it from rbi.org.in, dicgc.org.in or incometax.gov.in close to the exam date. Never state a figure you are not sure of — write 'verify' instead.
ga-accounts.blockPlan: A 90-minute block built around two tables. Minutes 0-25: hand-build Table 1 comparing savings, current, BSBDA, FD and RD across six columns — who can open, interest paid, minimum balance, transaction limits, tenor, and premature-withdrawal treatment. Minutes 25-45: hand-build Table 2 comparing NRE, NRO and FCNR(B) across currency, source of funds, permitted account types, taxability, repatriability and tenor. Minutes 45-60: on a separate card, write the numbers that get asked as bare figures — DICGC Rs 5 lakh, TDS Rs 50,000 and Rs 1 lakh at 10% (20% without PAN), tax-saver FD 5-year lock-in and Rs 1.5 lakh under 80C, small account Rs 50,000 balance and Rs 10,000 monthly withdrawal, four nominees from 1 November 2025, two years to inoperative and ten years to the DEA Fund. Minutes 60-80: close everything and rewrite both tables and the number card from memory, marking every miss. Minutes 80-90: attempt 15 questions from a current bank and log each error against the specific row that failed. Re-recite the number card weekly, and re-verify the tax thresholds and any nomination rules in the fortnight before 27 December 2026.
ga-accounts.weightageNote: This topic contributes nothing to Prelims, which has no General Awareness section. In Mains, General Awareness is 40 questions for 50 marks in 20 minutes, and deposit-account rules are a staple of its banking-awareness component, worth a small number of direct questions in a typical paper. Two features make it worth a dedicated block despite the modest count: the questions are pure recall answerable in 10-25 seconds, and the same facts underpin the banking-awareness questions in the interview and in other bank examinations. Confidence is marked medium because the tax thresholds and nomination rules changed recently and are subject to further statutory revision, so the figures must be re-verified before the exam.
ga-accounts.websiteRef: https://www.rbi.org.in (Master Directions and Master Circulars on interest rates on deposits, BSBDA and inoperative accounts; the UDGAM portal), https://www.dicgc.org.in (deposit insurance coverage, limits and exclusions) and https://www.incometax.gov.in (Section 194A thresholds and Forms 15G/15H)

ga-negotiable.topicName: Negotiable Instruments — Cheque, DD, Bill of Exchange
ga-negotiable.whatItIs: The Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 governs written instruments that carry a right to money and can be transferred by delivery or endorsement. The Act itself names exactly three: promissory note (Sec 4), bill of exchange (Sec 5) and cheque (Sec 6). A cheque is a bill of exchange drawn on a specified banker and payable on demand. Demand drafts, hundis and banker's cheques are treated as negotiable by usage/other provisions, not by a fresh definition in the Act. For IBPS Clerk Mains this is pure recall: definitions, parties, section numbers, the Section 138 timeline, crossing types, and the recent RBI cheque-clearing changes.
ga-negotiable.coreMethod:
1. Lock the three-instrument spine first: Sec 4 = promissory note (2 parties: maker, payee), Sec 5 = bill of exchange (3 parties: drawer, drawee/acceptor, payee), Sec 6 = cheque (3 parties: drawer = account holder, drawee = always the bank, payee). If you know only this, you can eliminate two options on most questions.
2. Build a one-page parties-and-differences table: cheque vs bill vs promissory note vs DD, on five columns — who draws, who pays, needs acceptance?, payable on demand?, can it be dishonoured for insufficient funds? DD is prepaid, so the last column is 'no' — that single cell answers a whole family of questions.
3. Memorise the number chain for dishonour as one string: 3-30-15-30-2-20. Cheque valid 3 months from its date; payee sends notice within 30 days of getting the bank's return memo; drawer has 15 days from receiving the notice to pay; complaint to be filed within 30 days (one month) after those 15 days lapse; punishment up to 2 years and/or fine up to twice the cheque amount; Sec 143A interim compensation up to 20% of the cheque amount (Sec 148: appellate court, minimum 20% of the fine/compensation).
4. Learn crossing as a ladder of increasing restriction, with sections: Sec 123 general crossing (two parallel transverse lines, must be paid into an account), Sec 124 special crossing (banker's name written in), Sec 126 effect of crossing, Sec 130 'not negotiable' crossing (transfer still possible, but the transferee gets no better title than the transferor), 'account payee' crossing (banking practice — NOT defined in the Act). Sec 131 protects the collecting banker, Sec 85 protects the paying banker.
5. Add the current-affairs layer, because Mains mixes static with recent RBI action: Positive Pay System (introduced by RBI in January 2021) — the issuer re-confirms cheque details electronically; banks were required to enable it for cheques of ₹50,000 and above and may make it compulsory for ₹5 lakh and above. RBI's continuous-clearing move under CTS ran in phases from October 2025, with the tighter confirmation window from 3 January 2026, bringing cheque realisation to same-day.
6. Attack pattern in the exam: scan the stem for the one anchor word — a section number, a rupee figure, a day-count, or a party name. Match it against your table. Do not read all five options first; read the stem, form your answer, then look for it among the five.
7. If the anchor does not fire within 15 seconds, skip. With 0.25 negative marking and 40 GA questions in 20 minutes, one blind guess costs more than the 30 seconds you save.
8. Worked example: 'A cheque dated 12 January 2026 is presented on 20 April 2026 and returned by the bank. The most likely reason is — (a) insufficient funds (b) stale/out-of-date cheque (c) post-dated cheque (d) material alteration (e) refer to drawer.' Validity is 3 months from the date written on the instrument, i.e. up to 12 April 2026. 20 April is past that, so the answer is (b).
tricks: Say the Section 138 timeline as one number-string '3-30-15-30-2' before you read the options. Questions on this topic almost always pick one of those five numbers, so having the whole chain loaded lets you reject four options in about five seconds instead of reasoning each one out.

On any cheque question, the drawee is the bank — never the payee, never the holder. Any option that names a person as drawee of a cheque is dead on sight, which typically kills one or two of the five distractors instantly.

A demand draft is prepaid by the purchaser, so it cannot bounce for want of funds and cannot attract Section 138. Any option that pairs 'DD' with 'dishonour for insufficiency of funds' or 'Section 138' is wrong without further thought.

Section numbers cluster in three blocks: 4-5-6 are the definitions, 123-131 are crossing plus banker protection, 138-148 are dishonour and its procedure. Placing an unfamiliar section number in its block tells you what the question is about even when you do not recall the exact section.

Days of grace (3 days, Sec 22) attach only to instruments payable at a fixed future date. A cheque is payable on demand, so grace days never apply to it — this settles the common 'how many days of grace on a cheque' distractor at zero.
traps: The three-month validity runs from the date written on the cheque, not from the date it was handed to you, not from the date it was signed, and not from the date of presentation. A cheque dated 5 March handed over on 20 March expires on 5 June, not 20 June.

Section 138 punishment is imprisonment up to two years, and fine up to twice the cheque amount. Papers routinely offer 'three years' and 'equal to the cheque amount' as distractors, and both are wrong.

The 15-day clock in Section 138 belongs to the drawer, and it starts from his receipt of the payee's notice — not from the date of dishonour and not from the date the notice was posted. The payee's own 30-day clock starts from information of dishonour from the bank.

A 'not negotiable' crossing under Section 130 does not make the cheque non-transferable. It stays transferable; what it removes is the transferee's ability to acquire a better title than the transferor had. The crossing that stops transfer in banking practice is 'account payee' — and account payee crossing finds no definition in the Act at all.

A bill of exchange needs acceptance by the drawee before he is liable; a cheque never needs acceptance because it is payable on demand. Options that say 'a cheque must be accepted by the bank before payment' are wrong.

Positive Pay is a customer-side confirmation of cheque details for large-value cheques; it is not a ban on small cheques, not a replacement for CTS, and not a Section 138 provision. Do not let the ₹50,000 / ₹5 lakh figures get attached to the wrong scheme.
ga-negotiable.timeTarget: GA gives 40 questions in 20 minutes — 30 seconds average, so factual banking questions must go in 10-15 seconds each. Budget 12 seconds for a direct section/number question and 20 seconds for a statement-combination question. Learning target: 45 minutes to build the table and number chain, then 10 minutes of revision per week.
ga-negotiable.masteryCheck: In 90 seconds, write from blank paper: (i) the three instruments defined in the NI Act with their section numbers; (ii) the parties to a cheque and to a bill of exchange; (iii) the string 3-30-15-30-2-20 fully expanded into sentences; (iv) four crossing types with sections, marking which one is not in the Act; (v) two ways a DD differs from a cheque. Then attempt 10 mixed five-option MCQs on this topic in under 3 minutes with at most one wrong and no blind guesses.
questionPatterns: Direct section recall with five section numbers as options — e.g. 'Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency of funds is dealt with under which section of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881? (a) Section 130 (b) Section 131 (c) Section 138 (d) Section 143 (e) Section 148' — answer (c).

Statement-combination with five combination options — e.g. three statements on crossing, with options 'Only I', 'Only I and II', 'Only II and III', 'All I, II and III', 'None of these'. The exam tests whether you know 'account payee is not defined in the Act' as the false statement.

Odd-one-out / NOT questions — 'Which of the following is NOT defined as a negotiable instrument under the NI Act, 1881?' with promissory note, bill of exchange, cheque, demand draft and truncated cheque as the five options; the answer turns on the Act naming only the first three.

Applied mini-scenario — a dated cheque presented after a given gap, or a drawer who fails to pay within the statutory window, with five outcome options; solved by the validity rule or the 15-day rule.
Current-affairs overlay — the threshold value for Positive Pay, or the month from which RBI's continuous cheque clearing took effect, offered against five numeric/date choices.
ga-negotiable.searchQuery: Negotiable Instruments Act 1881 section 138 143A cheque crossing sections 123 to 131 RBI positive pay continuous cheque clearing 2026 banking awareness
ga-negotiable.aiPrompt: Act as an IBPS Clerk Mains General Awareness question setter. Create 15 multiple-choice questions on negotiable instruments under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (promissory note, bill of exchange, cheque, demand draft), plus RBI's Positive Pay System and continuous cheque clearing. EVERY question must have EXACTLY FIVE options labelled (a), (b), (c), (d), (e) — this is the IBPS format; never give four. Mix these types: 5 direct section/number recall, 5 statement-combination questions where the five options are combinations such as 'Only I', 'Only II and III', 'All of these', 'None of these', and 5 short scenarios (cheque dates, dishonour timelines, crossing effects). Include at least two questions where the correct answer is 'None of these'. After all 15 questions, give an answer key with a one-line reason and, where relevant, the exact section number. Do not include any question whose answer is ambiguous or depends on bank-specific internal policy.
ga-negotiable.blockPlan: Slot this as a 45-minute GA block on one day plus two 10-minute revision touches. Block A (45 min): read the three definitions and build the parties table on paper, then memorise the 3-30-15-30-2-20 chain and the crossing ladder with sections. Revision 1 (10 min, 3 days later): reproduce the table from memory, then attempt 15 five-option MCQs. Revision 2 (10 min, 2 weeks later): only the number chain, section clusters and the DD-vs-cheque differences, plus the Positive Pay and continuous-clearing facts. In a 4-hour day this fits the 30-40 minute GA slot that should sit at the end of your session, after Quant and Reasoning.
